Decides whether a companion held in confinement can be sold, which under the current simplified rule is any companion that is not dead.

Rolls a percent chance, based on how many days the store's stock has aged, to decide whether the store replenishes its items.
Computes the gold price the store charges to buy a companion, based on the companion's base value and how many of that alignment are penned, using the engine's logarithmic price formula.

Sets the three game clock tick intervals (combat 1000 ms, ailment 4000 ms, play 250 ms) into the game state and emits a "Clock setup" message to the context.

At the start of a fight, each party member who has no combat order yet is given one derived from the combat setting (currently hardcoded to 0, which maps to no order), following the standing-orders rule R10.

Each engagement tick, it counts down the encounter timer, then either has a hostile group attack or rolls a Charisma-based check to turn a peaced group hostile when the selected character is near it.
Looks up the base hostile value for a monster alignment and character alignment pair from a two-dimensional table, with no game logic beyond the indexing itself.

Rolls a hostility check against a threshold computed from the base value and Charisma (floored at 1, via the logarithmic formula T = trunc(base − 7.5·ln(cha))), returning true when a d100 draw is strictly below that threshold.

Computes a monster's free-attack threshold from the difference between its Dexterity and the character's, with a floor of 5 and an optional cap of 98 that applies only when the level-change rule is in effect.
Gives the free round to monsters already engaged in combat (rule R25 of the Mordor SRD) by delegating to freeRoundAs with the "Moved" caller.

On a player's move, it grants a free combat round to the party when they are engaged, unless the move stayed in the same area, with the free round for a hostile room arrival and a capped one for leaving or changing level.
Asks the host to hold the display for a melee result by emitting a "Melee hold" message with the requested duration in milliseconds, since the core never reads the clock itself.

Computes the natural logarithm of a value, used by the game's melee rules (per VB Ln) in formulas such as the scaled-magnitude and protection calculations.
Returns a random integer from 0 up to but not including n, using one uniform draw from the RNG and the VB-style Int truncation.
Returns the ceiling of a floating-point value as a 32-bit integer by truncating with vbInt and adding one when the value is not already whole, a numeric helper with no game meaning of its own.

Checks that a group index is within the valid range from zero up to kMaxGroups, with no game meaning of its own.
Returns the index of the first group in the encounter that is still standing (per R5 of the melee rules), or -1 if no group is left standing.
Decides whether combat begins on arrival, returning false if the monster group is empty, its front monster is not hostile, or no members are still alive, and true otherwise (SRD c07p1 rule R1).
Decides whether a melee swing's aim must be re-chosen, returning true when the aimed group index is invalid or the group is no longer standing (SRD R2, R3, R5).

Returns true only when a character's combat order is None, implementing rule R4 that the combat setting applies only to characters with no order.

Computes a combatant's total swings per weapon for melee combat by adding the actor's Swings value to the weapon's Swings value (SRD c07p1, R7).
Implements the R8 no-weapon rule: if the actor has no weapon or total swings are below 1, it announces "Using no weapon!" and sets the actor's combat order to Defend, returning true.
Computes the number of extra swings a character earns from the Multiple Swings ladder, based on their Multiple Swings value and guild level, using the SRD's logarithmic threshold progression (R10).
Applies Mordor's R11 swing rule, where a guild's award replaces the current swing figure only when the award is higher, so swings never go down.
Returns true when a monster with the needs-good-weapon bit (R13/R15) is hit by a weapon whose floor is below half the monster's level found, meaning the weapon is too weak to affect it.

Converts a DamageKind enum value to a 64-bit unsigned integer index by casting it through a signed 32-bit int, with no game rule applied.
Clamps an integer to a minimum of zero, returning 0 for negative inputs and the value unchanged otherwise.
Totals the Def values of all currently equipped worn items in the player's inventory to give the character's overall defence bonus from armour.
Maps an alignment enum value (Good, Neutral, Evil) to its corresponding alignment bit constant, returning 0 for unrecognized values.

Computes a paralysed character's attack and defence values from base, best guild and equipped gear bonuses, with the stat term taken as zero and results floored at zero.
When paralysis at level 0 or a city-gate clear happens, the character's current stat shift is copied into the stored stat shift so it persists, and a "Stored stat shift kept." message is shown.
Reports whether a character's stat part is held, which is false when the character is paralysed and true otherwise, per game rule R6.

what: Sets or clears a character's Defend order in Mordor: when turned on, the character's order becomes Defend and their swing count is reset to zero so they stop attacking, and when turned off, the Defend order is removed if it is currently active, with a message to the player either way.
When a weapon has proven useless, this turns the character's Defend order on, so they defend instead of attacking.
Returns whether the character's Defend order is active, which in game terms makes that character harder to rob.
Takes the Defend-bonus value and returns it unchanged, ignoring the defend flag, because the original game's +50% Defend bonus is dead code and the port intentionally applies no bonus.
Looks up a race's base resistance to a given damage kind from the race table, returning 0 if the race or the resistance entry is missing, as the first step of the game's resistance calculation.
Checks whether any equipped item the wearer counts for carries a resistance flag matching the given damage kind, and returns true if so, which grants the character resistance to that damage type.
Returns the fixed resistance value of 90 when the gear grants resistance, since worn items replace rather than stack with the race's base resistance, otherwise it returns the race base.
Tests whether an item's resistance bitmask covers a given damage kind, returning true when the item resists that kind of damage and false if the kind is out of range.
Casting a resistance-raising spell out of combat sets the target's resistance to the matching damage kind to at least 95 percent, and refuses the cast during combat.

Maps a spell's class (Fire, Cold, Electrical, Mind, Damage, Kill, Banish, Dispel, Charm, Element, Protection) to the resistance category a target uses to defend against it, so the game's resistance rules apply correctly.

Computes the chance that a monster hits a character by comparing the monster's attack against the character's defense, shifting the base hit chance up or down by a spread proportional to the difference and clamping the result to a floor and ceiling.
Rolls a d100 against the monster's computed hit chance (from its attack and the character's defense) and returns whether the monster's attack hits.
On a player attack, it builds the hit-check arguments with the monster's Defense set to 0 and the character's Defense set to the given value (rule R19).
Reports whether a companion slot is a living participant in combat, meaning it is occupied, has Hits above zero, and is not dead.
Returns the absolute value of a 32-bit integer, a generic math helper with no game meaning.
Tests whether a given bit is set in a 32-bit flags word and returns true or false, a generic bit-manipulation helper with no game-specific meaning.
Returns the number of monster definitions loaded in the context's data, as an i32.
Returns a reference to the monster definition at the given index in the monster data table, cast from a signed to an unsigned index.
Scans the pen's shelf list and returns the index of the first shelf whose monster reference and alignment both match the given values, or -1 if none does.
Adds one unit to the stock count of a matching shelf in the pen (or creates a new shelf holding one unit if none matches), keyed by monster reference and alignment.

Finds the first of the character's four companion slots that is still empty (not occupied by a Companion), returning its index or -1 if all are filled, which the game uses when a companion joins the party.
Re-syncs a companion's stored monster reference by matching its monster ID against the monster table, falling back to the first entry with that ID and leaving the reference unchanged if none matches.
Maps a companion's alignment to the monster-table index for Id 307 (Morgul for Neutral or Good, Shadow Ninja for Evil), falling back to the Neutral reference if the table lacks Id 307.

Maps a stored companion alignment value (0 to 2) to the companion's alignment scheme by shifting it up by one, and otherwise falls back to the monster definition's alignment, per the SRD c12p1 companion rules.

Raises a companion's binding level by one step at Confinement, charging the owner gold based on the companion's guild level and current binding, and refuses if the companion is already at the life-binding level or the owner cannot pay.

what: Decides whether a non-engaged monster group may offer to join the viewing party, based on alignment match (or neutral) and whether the group's guild level is within the viewer's top guild level.
Computes a companion's join bar as Charisma times 10, reduced by 10 for each level above the first the monster was found at, floored at zero (per SRD c12p1).
Rolls a d3000 check against a Charisma-and-level-based join bar, and if the roll passes, picks which of up to four groups makes the join offer (group 0 is the only one shown).
Creates a new companion from the front monster in a party, copying its current and maximum Hits, identity, alignment, and level, and marking it as freely joined with the default free-will binding.
Refuses a dead character's attempt to join the party while monsters are present, per the SRD c12p1 join rule.
Rolls a d3000 percentile-style check against the player's Charisma minus a level penalty to decide whether a monster joins the party.
Computes the probability that a monster voluntarily joins the party as CHA minus monster level plus one, floored at zero, divided by 300.
Decides whether a Charm forces a companion to join the party, returning true when the damage inflicted in combat exceeds the monster's remaining hits (per R13.3 of the game's rules).
Records one rejected subtype draw for the companion's subtype selection, resetting the subtype to 0 after more than 150 tries and marking the pick as failed after more than 300.

Maps a monster spawn mode number to the spawn window (how far above or below the party's level a creature may come from) and to a fixed monster table entry, or to "lead itself," with modes 7 and negatives leaving the previous window unchanged.
Decides whether a companion is still able to act in combat, which is true only while its hit points are above zero (rule R22.1).
Counts how many of a character's four companion slots hold a living companion, meaning occupied, not dead, and with hits above zero (R22, R25.3).

Decides whether a companion's breath attack is blocked, returning true when a fire breath bit is set or when a cold breath bit is set and the cold breath has not already been blocked by an earlier breath.

Rolls the breath chance for a companion by comparing the lead foe's guild level to the companion's, returning 80 if the foe is more than a quarter stronger, 20 if it is more than a quarter weaker, and the base chance otherwise.
Computes the monster's breath range from its level and the character's level, using a seeded logarithmic formula that differs from the companion breath calculation.
Returns the total number of bodies in the party by adding the number of characters to the number of living companions.
Rolls a spit-odds mishap for a companion, and if it triggers, picks a random party member other than the owner to be struck, then reports the friendly-fire event to the player.
Does nothing: it takes a companion's spell-or-blow action and discards every argument, since the rule it would implement (R27) is not in this SRD excerpt.
Returns the absolute value of a 32-bit integer, with no game meaning.
Decides whether a companion may cast a spell this round, allowing it only if its owner's side has not already cast this round and anti-magic is not in effect (rule R27.1).
Spends one charge from the owner's item in the given pack slot to pay for a companion's cast, refusing with "Out of charges." if the slot is invalid or the item has none left.
After a companion casts, the owner's combat order becomes Defend if the companion's Att is 0 or 1, otherwise Fight (per R27.3).

In the Mordor rules (R27.5), a companion caster who is not a Mage has a fixed percentage chance (kCasterFizzlePercent, half the time) of their spell fizzling, which the function rolls on the context's RNG.
Rolls a percent chance (kCasterFailPercent, 50 per the R27.5 note) that a companion's spellcasting attempt fails.
Decides where a healing spell goes in the companion routine: nobody if the heal target flag is 0, monsters as damage if the heal was passed to a slot, and the party otherwise.
Reports whether a companion's body is magic-immune by returning the body's magicImmune flag, which stands in for the R27.7 test that the header says is not present in this part of the code.
Computes a companion spellcaster's mishap chance by multiplying the spell's odds by 1.5 and clamping the result between the game's floor and ceiling of 1 and 40.
Rolls a companion caster's spell mishap check by discarding one d100 draw, then comparing a second d100 roll against the spell's computed mishap chance and reporting whether the spell misfires.

Computes a companion's stoning chance from their Constitution and the level at which they were found, capping the result at 95%.

Rolls whether a stoning effect lands on a target by checking the target's stone resistance and then a chance derived from the stoner's Constitution and level, following the game's documented stoning formula.
Returns the index of the first creature in the foes list, at or after startIndex, whose hits are greater than zero, or -1 if none is alive.
Returns a constant 0 for the Electrocute damage formula, ignoring both level arguments, because the rule is not yet implemented in this part of the rules.

Applies the effects of a landed blow, possibly stoning the target (if the stone check succeeds) and electrocuting it for damage that is subtracted from its hits, and returns the electrocution damage dealt.
Plays the death-cry message "DI-UNDEA" on its own line for the player before the mishap line, unless suppressed.
Sends the "DRAGON" attack-cry message to the owner when a melee companion hits a party member without killing them, as a mishap event under rule R32.3.

Builds the "You were accidently hit for" or "You were accidently electrocuted for" caption naming the victim (plus "and his companions" when applicable) and sends it to the player, showing the hit caption only if the watched character was struck.
Returns true only when the slot being visited is the last slot visited, so the mishap suffix from R32.6 applies only to that final slot, since the suffix resets on each pass.
Reports a companion's kill to the mod/event system by emitting a "companion.kill" message for the owner character, without changing the owner's kill count.
Converts a companion's binding level into its bound value by taking the absolute value, multiplying by 4.5, and rounding half-to-even to an integer.
Rolls a random check against the companion's chance to leave and reports leaving if the roll succeeds or the companion's binding level is zero.
Casts an unsigned or wider integer index to a signed 32-bit integer, a pure type conversion with no game meaning.
Decides whether a companion is dead, which is true when its Hits are at or below zero or its dead flag is set.

Returns the slot index of the companion the player is carrying, or -1 if nothing or a body is carried, which the carry-choice logic uses to decide which companion is kept.
Decides whether the owner may choose a body for the carried item, which is allowed only when the carry slot is empty or holds a companion (carry index below the companion slot count).

Picks which occupied companion slot at 0 or fewer Hits is carried off, taking the first such slot and replacing it only with one of strictly greater MaxHits, so ties keep the earlier slot (rule R37.2).
Decides whether a creature of body size `bodySize` can be picked up by a carrier of size `carrierSize`, returning true when the size difference is at most 1 (per rule R37.3).

Runs the R37 carry choice for a fallen companion: it picks the healthiest-or-highest-max-hits downed companion, either picks it up as the carried body (clamping negative hits to 0) if it fits the carrier's size, or releases it as too big, and then sweeps the remaining fallen companions.
After a companion is kept in the carry choice, every other companion slot whose hit points have dropped to zero or below is cleared and marked released, per rule R37.4.
When a character dies, every occupied companion slot is released and the carried item index is cleared, so companions and carried items are lost.
Reports whether a companion has died, which the game's rules define as happening when the companion's Hits fall to zero or below.

what: Lets the player kick out a companion, refusing if it is dead (drop it first) or in the city, warning if it is bound, and only releasing it when the player has confirmed the Yes answer.
Decides whether a right-click attack on a companion is ignored (no HP left), refused (a Good companion checked against a Good comparison alignment), or lets the companion go.

When a companion is asked to attack by right-click, this checks whether the companion's alignment permits it, prints a refusal message if it won't, and otherwise sends the companion into combat as a forced action.

Decides whether a companion leaves the party to go with a creature, in the game's R41 "Let Companion Go" rule: it runs the turn check, and either stops, joins the creature's live set, or silently releases the companion's slot.
Scans the companion roster in order and returns the index of the first occupied slot whose hit points are zero, which is the candidate offered for raising at the morgue (or -1 if none qualifies).

Runs the Morgue raise attempt for a dead companion: charges the gold cost, rolls a chance based on the companion's Constitution to succeed, clears the owner's carried-character state, and either restores the companion to full Hits and Normal state or releases the slot empty.
If a companion's alignment is still Unaligned (encoded as 0), it adopts the alignment of its creature type, shifted by one to match the CompanionAlignment encoding.
When a companion's carry index is 4 or more (marking a carried body), it clears that index to kCarryNone so the body is put down when the game loads.
Finds the first unoccupied companion slot in the party's roster (the "hole" a new companion fills), returning its index or -1 if the roster is full.
When a new companion is placed into a slot, it inherits the name of the companion who previously occupied that slot.
Decides whether a monster of a given alignment may join a character of a given alignment: Good monsters join only Good characters, Neutral monsters join anyone, and Evil monsters never join.

Decides whether a monster is hostile to a character based on the monster's alignment: Good monsters attack anyone not Good, Neutral monsters attack on a rolled 60% chance, and Evil monsters always attack.
Charms a monster into becoming the caster's companion, placing it in a free companion slot as not freely joined, or reports that there is no room left.
Checks whether a character's Intelligence, Wisdom, Constitution, and Charisma all meet the minimum stat requirements for a given binding spell (Control, Bind, or Domination).
Returns true unless the companion joined freely, so that bind spells only take effect on companions who did not join of their own will (rule R49).

Applies a Bind-type spell to a companion: Control adds to its binding level, Bind or Domination raises it to at least the base level for that spell, and the result is capped at the maximum, or the spell does nothing if the companion can't be bound.
When a Control Dragon attempt fails, the target creature is flagged as hostile and the player is told that the dragon resists control.
Dominate Demon binds the demon to the player by setting its bound flag and raising its binding level to at least the Domination base level, then announces that the demon is bound.

Fills a companion slot from a monster, copying its identity, alignment, hits, and guild level, and setting its binding state (bound if the binding level is positive, ForLife at the maximum binding value) with all death, pending-raise, and release flags reset.
Computes the gold cost of binding a monster to a monster guild, scaling with the guild level and the absolute size of the current binding through a cost factor and a fixed cost unit.

Rolls a d3000 percentile-style check against the join bar computed from the target's charisma and found level, returning true when the roll is at or below the bar so the creature agrees to join the party.
Decides whether a monster group may offer to join the character by checking that the group's leader's alignment is Neutral or matches the viewer's alignment, via the engine's join rule.
Decides whether a monster can join a character based on alignment, where Neutral monsters can join any character and other monsters must match the character's alignment.
Renews a fading Bind on a companion by resetting a bound companion whose binding level is below base back to the base level, refusing if the companion is bound for life or joined freely.
Raises a companion's Bind level by the given amount, capped at the maximum of 100, and sets the companion to bound and ForLife at that cap, or refuses if the Bind is already ForLife.
Domination charm reduces the number of creatures a charm can affect in one group to the lower of the group count and the cap of four, returning zero for empty groups.
Charms a creature into a free companion slot of the caster, binding it at the starting binding for the target's floor and marking it as not freely joined, or refuses if no slot is free.
Computes the spit share for a group of living companions as N / (N + 1), returning zero when no companions are alive.
Returns the percent chance of a breath fire attack, at 80 if the lead foe's guild level is more than a quarter above the companion's, 20 if it is well below, and the base 50 otherwise.

Returns the total crit damage bonus for a companion by adding +4 if the crit-bit-10 flag is set and +1 if the crit-bit-11 flag is set in its special-property flags (R28).

Computes the damage a companion takes after resistance, reducing it by half the resist percentage (integer-truncated) of the incoming damage.

Rolls a percentile check against the companion's chance to leave (never true for ForLife companions), returning whether the companion departs.

Returns the death cry sound string ("DI-UNDEA") or the attack cry sound string ("DRAGON") depending on the flag, which are game-flavor sound names for companions.
Returns the index of the first empty companion slot (one whose ref is -1) for a new companion joining the party, or -1 if all four slots are occupied.

Returns the character's chance to leave the party, taken from the stored raw value and clamped to the allowed range the rules specify.

Computes the percentage chance that a creature turns on its master, based on the alignment gap between the creature and the master (0% for matching alignment, 100% for a two-step gap, and 75% or 15% for a one-step gap depending on whether the creature is Evil).

Rolls a turn-related chance check for a companion creature against its master, returning true or false based on a percentage derived from their alignments, with certain 0% and 100% outcomes short-circuiting the random draw.

Rolls a percent chance (currently a placeholder fixed at 50%) for a companion's friendly-fire attack, applying to every companion rather than only spitters.
Decides whether a breath attack is stopped, returning true only when it is a cold breath and an earlier breath was already made in the same round.

Compares a breather's power against a target's power and returns +1 if the breather is much stronger (more than 5/4 of the target), -1 if much weaker (less than 3/4 of the target), or 0 if the two are in between, for the breath relation rule [c28].

Returns 0 unconditionally for the join chance percent, since the CHA-by-level join chance table it needs has not been supplied yet, so no join chance is applied.

Returns true once the spawn try count reaches 300, serving as a guard against endless retries (rule [c7]), with no other game logic.

Does nothing: its body only discards both arguments, and it notes that the mood store it is meant to drift does not exist in Companion, so no state changes once per combat round.

Appends a 32-bit unsigned value to a byte vector as four little-endian bytes, least significant byte first.

Checks whether a new character can be created by testing, in order, that the name is non-empty, contains no forbidden bar character, that a sex and an alignment have been chosen, and that no save file already exists, returning the first failing reason or Ok.
Returns the entered password unchanged, with the Ctx argument ignored, because no rule text exists for how passwords are stored in the character record.
Sets a mod setting's text value in the in-memory settings store, updating an existing entry matched by mod id and key or appending a new one, and marks the store dirty.

Looks up a mod setting by mod ID and key in the settings store and returns its text, or the supplied default if no matching entry exists.
Removes every stored mod setting matching a given mod id and key, and marks the store as dirty only if something was actually removed.

Decodes text produced by modEncodeRows back into a grid of rows and cells, where backslash escapes the next character, "|" separates cells, ";" ends a row, and an unterminated final row is kept.
Builds a save tag by listing each live mod as "id@version", or returning a null tag when no mods are live.

Sets an item's identification level from a legacy boolean flag (identified maps to All, unidentified maps to Unknown) unless a modern known-level field is already present, in which case it does nothing.
Converts a character's gold balance into the save-file fields, recording the whole gold amount and setting a flag to store the exact value only when the balance has a fractional part.

Compares a guild's stored attack and defence values against the recomputed ones and, if they differ, emits a "guild.stats_differ" warning event to the player/game context listing the guild index and both sets of values.
Looks up a file name in two fixed lists and returns whether it is a vital data file, a non-vital one, or neither (unlisted).
Decides whether a data file may be deleted, allowing deletion only for files classed as non-vital (provisional rule, since the SRD deletion rule was not supplied).
Decides whether record 0 of a given MDATA table is kept when loading the game's table data, skipping only MDATA5's record 0 because it duplicates Outcast Goblin.

Converts a character slot index into a byte offset in the save/data file by adding the fixed first-record number (3) and multiplying by the 2900-byte character record length via the shared recordOffset helper.
Computes a flat index into the automap array from a dungeon level and x/y coordinates, using fixed offset and stride constants.
Returns true if the character is a space, tab, carriage return, or newline, which is generic text handling with no game meaning.
Converts a single ASCII uppercase letter to lowercase and returns every other character unchanged.
Returns the byte length of a byte vector as a signed 64-bit integer.
Returns true when a byte range starting at offset with length n lies fully within the buffer's bounds, guarding against negative values and overflow.
Grows a byte buffer with zero-filled bytes up to the requested size if it is currently smaller, leaving it unchanged otherwise.
Converts a signed 64-bit integer to its decimal string form, handling zero and negative values without relying on a library call.
Checks whether a string equals "true" under ASCII case-insensitive comparison, with no trimming, returning true only on an exact match.
Performs a case-sensitive linear scan of a string and returns true if it contains the character 'T', otherwise false.
Returns a copy of the input string with leading and trailing ASCII whitespace removed.
Reads a run of `count` little-endian 2-byte integers from a byte buffer into an output array, advancing the read position past each value.
Returns true when a config text value equals "True" ignoring case, which is a generic string-to-boolean parse with no game meaning of its own.

Returns true if the given string contains an uppercase 'T' (case-sensitive), which the game's welcome-flag check treats as "already welcomed," though the function itself is only a generic string test.
Returns whether the input string contains an uppercase 'T', a case-sensitive check that reports whether the limitation notice has been seen.

Returns the byte offset of character record n in the MDATA4 data file by delegating to a generic recordOffset helper with the character record length, which is a file-format calculation with no direct game meaning.

Maps the saved identification-level code from a data file (0 through 3, counting down) to the game's IdLevel enum, with codes 1 and 2 inferred rather than sourced and any other value mapped to Unknown.
Converts the legacy boolean "Identified" save flag into an identification level, mapping true to fully identified (All) and false to Unknown, per the SRD's c32 section.
Switches the character's active guild in Mordor, saving the current experience into the outgoing guild's membership record and loading the incoming guild's stored experience into the character.

Emits a warning message to the player (via ctx.say) that stored guild Att/Def values from a save or data file are being ignored and recomputed from guild level, with the guild and stored values attached as arguments.
Checks that a save file's race and guild names match entries in the loaded game data, reports each unknown name to the player, and returns whether both are valid so the load can be refused.
Looks up a legacy monster Id in the monster table and returns its index, refusing the ambiguous Id 307 and reporting it to the player via a message.
Checks whether a candidate character name would collide with an existing character's name once both are reduced to sanitised file names, so that two characters cannot end up sharing a save file.
Reads a 16-bit little-endian integer from a byte buffer at the given offset, returning false and zeroing the output if the read fails.

Reads a 4-byte little-endian unsigned integer from a byte buffer at a given offset, returning it through an out-parameter and reporting success or failure, with no game meaning.
Writes an unsigned integer into a byte buffer at a given offset as 1 to 8 little-endian bytes, growing the buffer as needed and silently doing nothing for invalid offsets or byte counts.
Writes a fixed-width byte field into a buffer at a given offset, truncating or space-padding the string to exactly n bytes, with no game meaning.
Returns whether the automap "been here" flag is set in a packed map word, meaning the party has already visited that square (per SRD c35).
Parses a binary guild-log file byte by byte into a list of GuildLogEntry records, each holding a guild index, a day serial stamp, and a text message, dropping any truncated tail.
Serializes a list of guild log entries (guild index, day-serial stamp, and text) into a little-endian byte buffer with a count header and length-prefixed text, for saving to a file.
Converts a monster table index to its file record number by adding a fixed base offset, with no game meaning of its own.

Returns true when the given pack slot index equals the reserved "Hands" slot constant, which never moves.

Reads one monster record from a binary buffer at a given offset, filling in its resistance, item-slot, box-chance and stat words plus the special property, special attack and spell flag longwords, and returns false if any read runs past the buffer.

Reads one 7-word stats-required run, a 7-word stat-mod run, and four 32-bit values (ability, alignment, resistance, charge) from a byte buffer at an offset into an item record, returning false if any read runs past the buffer.
Checks whether a given file number appears in the kVitalMdataFiles list and returns true or false accordingly.
Checks whether a given file number is in the list of regenerated mdata files, returning true if it is and false otherwise.
Builds the filename string "MDATA<n>.MDR" from a file number, a formatting helper with no game meaning.

Escapes a string for storage in a mod data row by replacing carriage returns and line feeds with spaces and backslash-escaping backslashes, pipes, and semicolons.
Joins a list of rows into one string, separating rows with ";" and cells with "|" and escaping each cell, with no game-specific meaning.

Reads a mod flag setting: if the key was absent it returns the fallback, otherwise it returns true only when the trimmed stored text is "True" in any letter case.
Formats a boolean as the text "True" or "False" for writing to data output, with no game-specific meaning.
Reports whether a key lookup in the game's data tables succeeded by inverting the "read was null" flag, so a key counts as present when the read returned a value.
Normalises a string value for writing by returning an empty string when the value is null and otherwise replacing each carriage return or line feed character with a space.
Builds a list of strings, one per live mod, each formatted as "id@version", for use as a save tag.
Returns the part of a string before the first '@' character (or the whole string if there is none), which is a plain text-splitting helper with no game meaning.
Returns the subset of tags whose mod id (via modIdOfTag) does not appear in the list of live ids, a generic list-membership filter with no game meaning.
Builds a string key of the form "itemId:alignment" by formatting the item id and the alignment's enum value as integers and joining them with a colon.
Returns the constant filename "settings.ini" as the port's replacement for MORDOR.INI, and never writes that file.
Returns true only when a key is missing from settings.ini, so the legacy MORDOR.INI file is consulted as a fallback for that key.
Converts a signed 32-bit integer to an unsigned 32-bit integer with a static cast, a general index-conversion helper with no game meaning.
Clamps a computed raise chance to the allowed band of 10 to 98 (using kRaiseChanceMin and kRaiseChanceMax), so a raise-the-dead success chance never falls outside the rule's limits.
Returns the absolute difference between two 32-bit integers, with no game meaning.
Charges a gold amount to the character, drawing from gold on hand first and then from the bank, and fails without charging if the character's total purse cannot cover it.

Shifts the "counted" flags for loaded party members down by one slot, starting at the given index, so a removed dead body drops out of the count of bodies that are still loaded, and clears the last slot.
Writes a guild log line recording a character's death, choosing "died somewhere" wording if the level is lost and "died on level N" otherwise.
Returns true when a character is dead and the party has been reduced to just that one member, which is the condition that triggers the dead-character screen under the game's rule R4.
Returns true when a character counts as a casualty of a party wipe, meaning their current hits are at or below zero or they are stoned (rule R5, step 2).

When the whole party is wiped out, it marks the casualties as dead (leaving stoned members stoned), logs the wipe as "dead in rock" or "dead in the dungeon," counts each newly dead character's death once, prunes the bodies if more than one remains, and flags the dead screen when a single body is left.
Decides whether the Wait button is offered on the death screen: it is enabled when the party is wiped, or when a party below ground has a dead member awaiting rescue.
When the player presses the wait button, it either ends an awaited rescue or, if the leader is dead, enters the rescue wait, returning true only when the rescue wait is entered.
Returns true when a character's current hit points are zero or below, which marks them as a casualty of the update step in the game's death rules (R6).

Records an ordinary death for a character by zeroing their hit points, clearing paralysis, poison, disease, and resistances, releasing any carried-character link, marking them Dead unless they are Stoned, and incrementing their death count and logging it.

Returns true unless the character is dead, enforcing the SRD rule (R7 step 9) that dead characters cannot rest while waiting.

Placeholder that does nothing: it takes a character and a context, discards both, and leaves the character's CON unchanged because the race minimum table it would need is not available.

Pays a rescue hire's cost from the gold leader's wallet, refusing the hire if no valid gold leader exists or the wallet cannot cover the cost.

Decides whether a fallen character's body can be recovered for rescue: it is never recoverable while in rock, always recoverable if dead, and for a living body only when current hits are at or below the rescue fraction (20%) of max hits.

Decides whether a dead character's body can be asked to rejoin the party, refusing if combat is ongoing, if the body is being carried, or if no Resurrect-based raise is pending, and otherwise allowing it.

Resolves a pending raise when a body is offered to rejoin the party, refusing if the body can't be raised (in combat or being carried), leaving the raise intact on a decline, and otherwise rolling the stored raise kind and chance to set the character as Raised or Failed.

Returns the current hit points a character is raised with, which is full max hits for a Resurrect or Morgue raise and 1 hit point otherwise.

Does nothing: it returns early for non-Morgue raises, and for Morgue raises it discards its arguments and applies no CON loss because the probability is unknown, drawing no RNG.

Decides whether the morgue guild pays a raise cost for a character, which it does when the character's top guild level is 5 or lower and their total purse (on hand plus bank) is less than the cost.
Returns true when the party's carrying slot holds a dead character, which blocks the companion raise (rule R16.1: a caster carrying a character cannot raise).

Builds the list of companion slots that a caster can try to raise from the dead, keeping only dead companions that aren't carried, aren't already pending a raise, aren't the caster, and are on the same dungeon level and area as the party.
Puts down the companion the party is carrying, clearing the carrying slot and companion index silently, as the rules require when a death occurs (R16.4).
Returns the Constitution stat used for a companion's raise-dead rule (R16.3), taking the companion's own CON score when its monster definition exists and a fixed fallback value otherwise.
Rolls a d100-style check against the companion's morgue chance (derived from natural Constitution) to decide whether a companion's raise from the morgue succeeds, returning true on success.
Marks a party member as dead in the given death state and queues a "has died" message for the player, with the original's cleanup step left unimplemented.
When the party falls out of the sky, it kills every member with an ordinary death (with a tell box shown for each) and then displays the message "You fall out of the sky!" to the player.

When the party leader is at zero hits, this checks whether a chest's trap has killed the party: if the leader is still standing nothing happens, otherwise the opener is killed if they are in the leader slot and not already dead, and the chest's gold is left untouched.
Computes a character's age as a percentage of their race's lifespan (age in years divided by lifespan, times 100), returning 0 if the lifespan is non-positive, which feeds the old-age death check.

Rolls the old-age death check for a character past 98% of the age threshold, where the chance of dying rises with the excess percentage via a logarithmic formula (5 + Ln(pct − 98) out of 100), skipping the roll when the excess is zero.
Offers each of the character's six natural stat values to the Hall of Records as a stat-category entry, logging them as solo records for the new character.
When a monster is killed, the killer's active guild monster quest is marked Done if its target matches that monster, and a completion message naming the character is produced.
Placeholder that marks the Hall of Records as dirty and always returns false without recording anything, because the comparison against the hall's record fields is not implemented.

Computes the hall date field for the game's date display as days since 1900-01-01 plus a fixed offset (R22).
Checks whether a dead character can be retrieved from the soul list, returning an error if the character is on a different dungeon level or not dead in rock in area 0, and Ok otherwise.
Splits a comma-separated coordinate string into its parts, dropping a single trailing comma, and returns the pieces as a vector of strings.
Computes the percentage chance of losing CON on a raise, as 50 minus twice the character's natural CON, floored at zero.
Computes the morgue Constitution-loss roll threshold for a character, which is 50 minus twice their CON, so high-CON characters effectively never lose CON there.
Rolls a percentile check against a threshold to decide whether a character loses one point of natural Constitution during a raise, following rule R26.
Rolls the stone-path CON-loss check for a raise by looking up the character's natural Constitution and running the loss roll against the chance derived from it, per SRD R26.
Rolls the CON-loss check for the morgue path (kind 23) using the character's natural Constitution score against a threshold derived from that score, which can cost the character Constitution.
Computes a character's age as a percentage of their race's maximum lifespan (R36), returning 0 when the race has no lifespan, which feeds the old-age death check.
Computes the old-age death chance threshold for a character at a given percent of max age, which is 5 plus the natural log of how far past 98% the character is, returning 0 at or below 98%.
Returns true only when the character is in the dungeon and their age percentage of race lifespan exceeds the start threshold (98%), which is when the random old-age death check begins.
Rolls the old-age death check for a character in the dungeon, and if the roll succeeds, marks the character as Dead and announces it to the player.
Finds the index of the party member that matches a picked character, first by object identity and then by name, returning -1 if no match is found.
Computes the character's natural Constitution, the stored CON stat with no modifier applied, which the morgue, raise, and revival chances use as their input.
Computes the morgue-counter chance for a character's own body in Mordor, taken as the character's natural Constitution plus a fixed bonus and clamped to the allowed raise-chance range.
Picks the chance that a character is recovered from the morgue, using the route taken (their own body or a morgue counter) to choose which chance calculation applies.

Returns the given currency amount with its fractional part dropped, by converting it to whole gold and back.

Returns a read-only reference to the square at grid coordinates (x, y) in a floor's square array, converting the coordinates to a flat index via cellOf.

Returns the party leader's ability-5 score (stat plus stat modifier, approximated since the real BestAbilityValue is unavailable), which is used as the value for the entry secret-door roll (R16) in the dungeon.
Reports a wall collision by showing an "OUCH" message through the context's say hook, with no game-text body, as a plugin-style output hook.

Converts a 1-based (x, y) map coordinate into a flat square index using row-major layout with the map width of 30.
Returns the wall/feature flags for a given dungeon square (numbered from 1), or 0 if the square is out of range, following the game's rule that a square's walls come from its field entry.
Returns whether the party's map is active, which is true unless the leader is lost (the game's nav.Mapping rule: automapping stops when the leader becomes lost).

On arrival at a square, if the leader is lost, it ends the lost state when the square is already mapped, and otherwise lets the party try to work out where they are, then syncs the party's lost flags.

Applies the R29 rotator trap check: if the character's ability-5 chance fails to beat a random roll scaled by dungeon level, the character becomes lost, with position and facing unknown.

Clears all three lost flags (level, position, facing) on the party's lost state when a morgue visit occurs, per SRD rule R32, without any message to the player.

Applies the effects of the square the party stands on after a move in the Mordor dungeon, including rolling a random facing for rotators, resolving pit falls, and announcing stairs, while leaving water/quicksand costs and teleporter/chute handling to other modules.
Clears every party member's protection masks and all eleven protection values to zero, then announces that the party's protections are extinguished.

Checks whether a spell is being cast on an anti-magic square and, if so, marks that square and tells the player "Anti-Magic area!", blocking the cast.

Returns true only when the area id is positive, which the rules (R47) use to decide whether random encounters can occur in that area.

When a body that was saved on a rock square is loaded, it is placed back onto that rock square's body list and a message announces that a body lies on the rock, provided the square exists and is rock.

Returns true only if the party has at least one member and the first member (party index 0, the leader) is alive, which gates whether the ask-to-join rule (R122) can proceed.
Converts a single ASCII uppercase letter to lowercase and returns every other character unchanged.

Finds the next loaded, enabled mod hook at or after the given index, in load order, so that hooks run in the order the mods were loaded; returns -1 if none remain.

Ends an action run by closing the current context and marking the run as no longer active.
Moves the party out of the dungeon and into town when they climb the stairs, placing the leader at the party's square on town level 0 and printing the "You climb the stairs to town." message.
Checks whether a party can continue an in-progress stair climb, which is allowed only while the party is still on the stairs and still inside the dungeon (rule R124).
Checks whether monsters are present in the party's current area, returning true if any party foe is alive, any living foe sits in the leader's area, or the leader's area has a standing monster group.

Refuses a user-initiated window close by showing the player a message telling them to use the Mordor EXIT buttons to leave the game.

Decides whether the player may exit the dungeon, refusing with a "Cannot exit while monsters are in the area!" message if monsters are nearby while the character is alive and below ground, otherwise prompting "Exit Mordor?" and returning a confirm outcome.
Given the party's position, it looks up the square the party stands on and reports whether a Take press would use stairs (up or down), a chute, or nothing.

Returns the area ID of the square at a given index on the lower floor, or -1 if the index is invalid.

Handles the player's chute-take action: refuses it on a dead-end level, otherwise drops every party member and the party itself down by the chute depth and prints the "You drop down the chute" message.

Decides whether a teleporter destination square can be drawn, rejecting any square that is out of range, recorded as rock, or holds a teleporter.

When the player fires a buffer with Shift during combat, it decides whether an item is used, a spell is cast immediately, a spell becomes a standing order, or nothing happens, based on whether monsters are present, whether the fight continues, and the spell-use disposition.

Returns the standing combat order (none, fight, defend, or spell:<id>) that a party member has set for the combat round, defaulting to "none" when no order is stored.
Clears the standing combat order for a party member when a fight ends, leaving that member's CombatSetting unchanged.

When a fight starts, it applies a member's CombatSetting to set their standing order to fight, defend, or a recorded spell buffer, or clears the order, and reports whether a pack item should be used instead.

When the player holds Shift and presses a buffer key during combat, it decides whether that buffer slot fires a spell, uses an item, or becomes a standing order, and records the standing order in featureState.
Registers the "buffer" player command on both the Town and Combat screens, so a player can set or list spell buffers for a party member with the usage line shown in help.
Converts a 32-bit integer to its decimal string form, with no game meaning.
Parses a string of one or two decimal digits into an integer, returning false if the text is empty, too long, or contains any non-digit character.
Parses a text string into a 1-based party member number and returns true only if the number is between 1 and the maximum party size.
Parses a text string into a 1-based companion slot number and reports whether it is a valid number within the allowed slot range, with no game mechanic applied.
Reports whether a companion slot is in use, meaning it is marked occupied and refers to an actual creature.
Reports whether a companion is fallen, meaning it occupies a filled slot and has zero or fewer hit points.
Decides whether the owner may choose a body to carry, allowing it only when the carry slot is empty or holds a companion (slot index below kCompanionSlots), and refusing when a morgue body is held.
Returns true when a companion's carry-slot index equals the given slot0 value, which tests whether that companion is occupying the specified carried-item slot.
Fills a CompanionsTarget with the member, inventory, and companion-slot records for a given member index and returns whether all three were found.
Returns a copy of the given string with any trailing space characters removed.

Releases a companion from a party slot, clearing its occupied flag and setting its creature reference to -1 while keeping its hit points and other fields, and returns a message saying it was let go (or that the member, slot, or empty slot is invalid).

Maps the companion's idLevel (how much the player knows about them, with 0 meaning fully known) to the display text shown in the Companion Information screen, such as "You know All" or "You know Nothing".
Builds the line of companion-drift text shown to the player when a companion's binding to its owner weakens by one level but stays at or above zero.
Applies one monthly-style drift tick to a companion's binding value: if the binding isn't yet "for life," a random roll against the drift score may nudge it one step toward zero.
Emits the companion drift message to the player through the event sink, but only when the companion's binding is zero or higher.

Handles the typed "companions <member>" command by checking the argument, then replying with that party member's list of up to four companion slots showing each one's name, hits, and whether it is being carried.

Rearranges a companion's party slots by swapping the two chosen slots' records, and moves the carry marker along with whichever companion it was holding, if the command's member/slot arguments are valid.
Handles the player's typed "release <member> <slot>" command by validating its arguments and either returning a usage message or releasing the chosen companion slot in the session.

Handles the player's typed "carry <member> <slot>" command, validating the member and slot, refusing when the target can't be picked up, and otherwise setting the carried companion and producing the player-facing message.

Registers the town and dungeon player commands "companions", "rearrange", "release", and "carry" so each one can be typed on those screens to list, reorder, release, or carry a party member's companions.
Parses a string of up to six plain decimal digits into an integer without throwing exceptions, returning false if the string is empty, too long, or contains any non-digit character.
Checks that a word parses as a plain decimal integer and that the result falls in the range 1 to kPartyMaxSize, returning the parsed party-member number through the out-parameter.
Checks whether a typed word is a valid companion slot number from 1 to kCompanionSlots, and the slots are fixed in place (never compacted) per rule R67.
Converts a 64-bit signed integer to its plain decimal text form with a leading minus sign for negatives, without relying on a standard library formatting call.
Converts a currency amount stored in 1/10000 gold into whole gold and formats it as text for display in the confinement (pens) screens.
Maps a pen alignment index (0, 1, or 2) to its display name, Good, Neutral, or Evil, for the confinement pens in Mordor's rules.
Returns the level used as the base for the guild level in the pen listing, taking the first party member's level or 1 when the party is empty.

Buys the chosen pen row for a party member by taking payment through confinementBuy, then fills the member's first free companion slot with the purchased creature and reports the price paid and remaining gold, or refuses with a message if the row, member, slot, or funds are invalid.

Handles the player's pen-sell command for a companion, refusing empty or invalid slots, running the confinement sale, and producing the reply text that reports the gold received and that the slot is now empty.
Handles the Confinement pens command by listing each penned monster with its alignment, count, and current buy price in gold, or reporting that the pens are empty.
Parses the typed "pen buy <row> <member>" command, validating its arguments and producing the player's error messages before handing the purchase to the confinement-buy routine.

Handles the typed `pen sell <slot> <member>` command by validating its argument count and parsing the companion slot and party position, then asks the confinement logic to sell that slot's companion, or replies with a usage or range error.
Dispatches the player's typed "pen" command to either the buy or sell handler, and returns a usage message when the command is missing or malformed.
Registers the town-screen player commands "pens" (lists the creatures in the Confinement pens with their buy prices) and "pen" (buys or sells a companion from those pens).
Parses a string of digits into a non-negative integer for a 1-based party member number, returning 0 if the string is empty, too long, or contains any non-digit character.
Joins the words of a token list from a given start index into one string separated by single spaces, which is used to rebuild a spell name or id from the typed command.
Depth Perception (SpellEffect 12) announces to the party the dungeon level they are currently standing on, as the spell's applied effect.
Find Direction (reference effect 13) reports the party's current facing as a compass code in a spell-cast message for dcast.
Registers the "cast" dungeon-screen command, which lets a player cast a non-combat spell for a party member by typed name or id, and wires it to the dcastRun handler.
Maps a trap number (0–10) to its display name as the original game prints it, returning "Unknown Trap" for anything outside that range.
Returns the guild level of the character's currently active guild, or 0 if no guild is active or the guild index is out of range.
Parses the second word of a typed command as a 1-based party member number and checks that it falls within the current party size, returning whether it is valid.
Returns the chest on the party's current square if one is present, or nullptr in town or when no chest exists, which the disarm and inspect actions use to find the trap target.
Handles the player's "inspect" command on a chest in the current square, replying with whether a chest is present, whether it is trapped, and the name of the trap if so.

Handles the typed `disarm <member>` command by checking for a chest on the current square and trapped status, then replies with a message, and does not perform the disarm roll or change the chest because it lacks the rng context needed.

Resolves a player's disarm attempt on a chest in the game: on success it awards experience to the acting member and clears the trap, on failure it clears the trap and reports that it went off, returning a message for the player.

what: Registers the typed "inspect" and "disarm <member>" commands for the dungeon screen, so the player can check a chest's trap or attempt to disarm it.
Returns the absolute value of a 32-bit integer.
Parses a string of digits into a non-negative integer, rejecting empty strings, signs, non-digit characters, and values above 100000.
Returns the one-line usage string for the `use` command, telling the player the syntax `use <member> <slot>` and that it uses an item from a pack slot (potions heal, scrolls cast).
Appends a line to a newline-separated reply string, inserting a newline first when the reply is already non-empty.

Returns an item's alignment as an integer, which the item-use code uses in its Mordor game-rule checks.
Returns a character's alignment as an integer, which the item-use code reads when checking whether an item's alignment restriction applies to that character.
Enforces the alignment rule for spells cast from an aligned item: the item only works for a character of its own alignment, and any other use fails with "Nothing Happens."

Computes how well an item's alignment fits the character's alignment, returning Same, Adjacent, or Opposed (Good, Neutral, Evil on a line, so one step apart is Adjacent and two steps is Opposed), which ApplySpecial uses to decide whether the item's effect applies.
Placeholder that takes a character and item definition, ignores them, and always returns false, since the permanent stat modifiers for Kind 1 items are not yet implemented.
Spends spell points by adding the given amount to the character's current spell points, capped at their maximum, as from a Scroll of Spells or Tome of Spells.
Applies the Potion of Youth / Dragon's Blood effect by subtracting the given number of years (converted to days) from the character's age, with the age clamped so it never goes below zero.

Placeholder for the item spell cast in the item-use feature: it does nothing and always returns false, pending an item cast entry point that would make a heal potion heal and a scroll cast.

Applies a player's use of an item from a party member's pack in Mordor: checks whether the item can be used, spends one charge (removing the item if it runs out), then casts its spell and applies its special effect such as spell points, aging, or stat modifiers.

what: Dungeon-mode command entry point that hands a typed `use <member> <slot>` command to the shared item-use handler, which applies the item's effect and produces the reply for the player.

Exposes a test-only wrapper that forwards its arguments unchanged to duseUse, the real implementation of the `use` verb, so it has no game logic of its own.

Registers the "use" dungeon command and the "useitem" town command, which let a player use an item from a party member's pack slot (potions heal, scrolls cast) and route to the handlers that do the work.
Returns true if a character is a space or tab, a whitespace test used when parsing the give command's arguments; it has no game meaning of its own.

Parses a typed gold amount as VB's CLng would, accepting optional sign and blanks, rejecting anything else (including thousands separators), and rounding half to even to a whole gold value.
Parses a typed party-member number from command text and checks it lies within 1 to the party size limit, reporting failure otherwise.
Validates a typed gold amount for a give-gold command, refusing it if it exceeds the gold held and otherwise converting it into the internal gold units to hand over.

Validates a typed item-give target by parsing the text as a number and accepting it only if it names a pack slot from 2 to kPackSlots (slot 1 is the Hands), returning that slot or -1 for "No Item to give!".
Returns the first empty pack slot (slots 2 onward, skipping the Hands in slot 1) for a party member, or nullptr if the pack is full.
Parses a typed "give" command and routes it to the gold or item handler, replying with usage text when the subcommand is missing or unrecognized.
Dispatches the player's typed `give gold ...` or `give item ...` command to the session's command handler and returns whether a reply message was produced.
Registers the "give" command for the Town and Dungeon screens, so a player can type "give gold" or "give item" to hand gold or a pack item to another party member.

Parses a decimal integer string (with optional leading minus) into a 64-bit value, setting an ok flag to false if any character is not a digit.
Returns a copy of the string with leading and trailing spaces and tabs removed, or an empty string if it contains nothing else.
Returns the current guild-log day counter from the session's feature state, or 0 if the value is missing or not a valid integer.
Reports how many guild halls exist in the game session, capped at the fixed guild count constant (kGuildCount).
Returns the trimmed name of a guild by index, or the bare number as text if the index is out of range.

what: Returns the trimmed name of the party leader (member 1) to sign the clean guild log record, or an empty string when there is no party.
Builds the string key "guildlog.e<index>" used to store a guild log entry at the given index in the feature state.
Serializes a GuildlogRow into a single pipe-delimited text line of guild number, day, and entry text.
Splits a raw pipe-delimited string into a guild number, a day number, and trailing text, returning false if the fields don't parse.
Reads the guildlog entry count from session state and unpacks each stored entry in order, skipping any damaged records, to return the guild log rows oldest first.
Replaces the entire stored guild log with the given rows by writing each entry under its indexed key, erasing leftover keys from the previous longer log, and updating the stored count.
Builds the label shown beside a guild log entry ("TODAY: ", "1 DAY AGO: ", or "N DAYS AGO: ") from the absolute number of days between the entry's day and the current day.
Joins the words from index `from` onward into one space-separated string, which is how a guild name given as several words is rebuilt from the typed command.
Resolves a player-typed guild argument, trimmed and case-insensitive, to a valid guild index either by number or by guild name, returning false if neither matches.
Reports whether the guild log has grown past its cleaning threshold, which is fifty entries per guild across the whole log (with at least one guild counted).

Serializes a list of removed guildlog rows into a text block (header, leader name, then guild, day and text per row) and stores it back in the session's guildlog text, which is a file-format writer rather than a game rule.

Handles the player's guild log cleaning command: if the log is over its threshold, it archives all but the newest kept entries to guildlog.text, rewrites the log with only those, and tells the player how many entries were removed.
Formats the guild appointment message by trimming a name and wrapping it in quotes with the sentence "was appointed GuildMaster."
Appends a new guild log entry, recording the guild, the game day, and the text, to the stored guild log.
When a new game starts, appoints each seeded guildmaster by writing an "appointed" entry for their guild into the guild log, once per session.
Registers the "guildlog" town command, which lets the player view a guild's log or clean it down to the newest 50 entries.
Maps a record index (0–11) to its display name and a descriptive label for the Hall of Records, falling back to "Master of Thieving" for any other index.
Builds the string key "hall.<k>.<field>" used to store and look up a Hall of Records entry's field in the game's feature state.
Looks up a string value in the session's feature-state map by hall record index and field name, returning the stored string or an empty string if absent.
Parses a decimal integer from text, accepting an optional leading minus sign and stopping at the first non-digit, returning 0 for unreadable input.

Reads a named integer field for one of the twelve Hall of Records entries from session feature state and parses it into a number, which the hall check and description logic use to compare or show records.
Returns a copy of a string with trailing space characters removed.
Formats a currency amount stored in 1/10000 gold as a plain decimal string with no trailing zeros, such as "0.25" or "-3".
Formats a Hall of Records value as display text, showing a creature id for the deadliest-creature record, gold for the wealthiest, a percentage for skill records, and a plain number otherwise.

Returns the value a character contributes to one of the Hall of Records categories (maxHits for Constitution, total experience for Most Experience, gold on hand plus in bank for Wealthiest, otherwise the matching ability score).
Builds the text block shown on the Hall of Records screen for one record, giving its heading, who set it (with the day number or the original holder), and its formatted value.

Offers a score to one of the twelve Hall of Records slots and, if the score beats the current record, stores the new holder, key, value and day, returning an announcement flag so the game can show the "just set the record" message (silent for self-improvement and for the deadliest-creature record).
Shows the player the Hall of Records by building a header line plus one description line for each of the twelve records and returning the combined text as the reply.

On a party's arrival in town, offers each living-or-dead party member to the Hall of Records and returns the announcement lines for any records they set, using a per-record offer value and a check that records the new best.

When a player's character kills a monster, it offers that monster to the Hall of Records as a candidate for the "Deadliest Creature" record, comparing its power against the current holder and noting whether the party was solo.

Registers the "hall" town command, which opens the Hall of Records screen showing the twelve town-wide bests (strength, intelligence, and so on through thieving, plus deadliest creature, most experience, and wealthiest).
Returns a copy of the given string with every lowercase ASCII letter converted to uppercase, leaving other characters unchanged.
Parses a non-negative decimal integer from a string, returning the fallback value if the string is empty, contains a non-digit character, or exceeds 1,000,000.
Joins the words of a string vector from a given index onward into one space-separated string.

Looks up a stored knowledge record for a given monster or item kind and name in the session's feature state and returns the requested field (such as a knowledge grade), or an empty string if no record exists.
Returns the name string at index i from a fixed-size array of names, or an empty string if the index is out of range.
Joins the names of the set bits in a bitmask into one comma-separated string, using the matching entries of a name array.
Builds the library page text for an item entry, listing its abilities if the entry is fully known and otherwise showing a "Not everything is known." notice.
Chooses which library page to show for a knowledge entry, sending monster entries to the monster page builder and everything else to the item page builder.
Searches a list of library entries for one whose kind and name match the given values, ignoring case in the name, and copies the first match into the output parameter.
Registers the "library" town-screen command, which lets the party look up what it has learned about monsters and items (or search its knowledge) by typed subcommand.
Converts a 64-bit integer to its decimal string form, with no game meaning.
Pads or truncates a string to a fixed width by trailing-space padding, used to lay out columns on the Look page.
Reports whether a character is dead by checking that their death state is anything other than Alive, which the game's rules use to gate actions like looting, climbing, and chest opening.
Looks up the guild name for a character's active guild from the loaded game data, returning an empty string if the guild index is out of range.
Converts a facing index (0–3) to its compass letter N, E, S, or W, returning "?" for any out-of-range value.
Builds the list of party members in the current room for the Look-around page, counting living members and dead non-leader members separately.
Builds the one-line readout for the Look page showing the party's x,y coordinates, dungeon level, facing letter, and living count with an optional "+dead" suffix.
Handles the typed "look" command by rejecting extra arguments with a usage message, otherwise returning the Look page text for the current session.
Registers the "look" typed command on the Dungeon screen, binding it to the cmdLook handler so the player can describe the square they stand on.
Returns a copy of the given string with every character converted to lowercase, which is general text handling with no game meaning.
Compares two strings for equality ignoring case, used to match a typed word against an option or command name (such as an INI key) without regard to capitalization.
Returns the index of the first entry in a list of names that matches a given word, ignoring case, or -1 if none match.
Returns true if a string is non-empty and made up entirely of ASCII digits '0' through '9', otherwise false.
Parses a case-insensitive text token ("on/true/yes/1" or "off/false/no/0") into a bool, returning false if the text is not a recognized boolean word.
Parses a string of up to three digits into an integer and rejects it if it exceeds the level maximum, returning success or failure without any game-specific effect.
Parses a string as a decimal party slot number, returning its value if it is between 1 and kPartyMaxSize and -1 otherwise.
Builds the INI key string for a game option by prefixing the given name with "option.".
Builds the INI key string "option.charN.name" by prefixing "option.char", appending the member index as a digit, and then the name, with no game logic involved.
Looks up a key in the session's feature-state map and returns the stored string value, or the supplied default if the key is absent.
Returns the on/off display text for one of the twelve game option checkboxes, reading its stored "1" or "0" value from the session and mapping it to "on" or "off".
Returns the stored text value for a game-option integer field by looking up its INI key, falling back to "(default)" for the volume field and "0" for the others.
Returns "on" or "off" for a character's boolean option, reading the stored INI value for that member and key (falling back to the default), for display in the character command and option listings.
Returns a constant usage string describing the syntax of the "options" command (with its name, member, and value forms), with no game mechanic applied.
Builds the text listing of all game options for the player, showing each boolean and integer setting, the last backup date, and every party member's character options.
Handles the player's typed options command in the game, either reporting the current value of a named option or setting it on or off, or to a number from 0 to 100, and returns the message to show.
