Builds the gear-screen summary line showing a character's combat attack/defence and total attack and defence, derived from the character and inventory in game terms.
Checks whether a player-typed pack slot is a real item slot, refusing slot 1 because it is the character's hands rather than an item, and sets the refusal message the player sees.
Parses a typed town command (help, rest, guild, levelup, join, shop, buy, sell, bank, equip/unequip/use) and routes it to the matching town action, replying with the result or a usage line.

Charges a party member the identify fee from their purse to identify one pack item, after validating the member and slot numbers and reporting whether the item was identified, already known, unaffordable, or empty.
Validates that the chosen party member exists and is dead, then tells the player that raising them is not available yet, since the morgue fee, success roll and consequences are not implemented.
Checks whether a string is non-empty and made up only of ASCII digit characters '0'–'9', returning true or false.
Normalizes a text string for case-insensitive comparison by trimming leading and trailing spaces and lowercasing ASCII letters.
Joins the words in a string vector from index `from` up to (but not including) `to`, separating them with single spaces, and returns the result.
Looks up a spell in the game data by case-insensitive name match first, then by numeric id if the text is all digits, and returns a pointer to it or nullptr.
Looks up a spell definition by its numeric id in the game data's spell list and returns a pointer to it, or null if no spell has that id.
Resolves a member word typed in a "spells <member>" command to a 0-based party index, accepting either a 1-based party position or a member name, and returns -1 if no valid member matches.

Handles the player's typed "spells <member>" town command by validating the member number, then replies with the spells that member can reach along with each spell's SP cost and whether it's usable in combat or town.
stageB_where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.RefreshSheetSpells (or Mordor.Core/SpellBuffers.cs SpellBuffers.CostText for the per-spell cost)

what: Handles the town-menu "cast" command by parsing the typed member, spell name, and optional group, checking the caster is alive, reachable, and has enough spell points, then spending the SP and reporting that the non-combat spell effect is not yet applied.
stageB_where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs box.CastSpellHere (with box.CastAndThrow and DungeonContext.Cast in Mordor.Modding/ModApi.cs as related paths)

what: Converts a 64-bit integer to its decimal string form, prefixing a minus sign for negatives, with no game meaning.
Formats a signed i64 amount stored in 1/10000 gold as a decimal string "G.FFFF" with zero-padded four-digit fractional part and a leading minus for negatives.
Maps a Race enum value to its display name string ("Human", "Elf", ..., "Troll"), returning "?" for unrecognized values.
Maps a Guild enum value to its display name string, returning "?" for unrecognized values.
Maps the Align enum (Good, Neutral, Evil) to its display string, returning "?" for any unknown value.
Maps the DeathState enum to its lowercase display name string (e.g., Dead becomes "dead"), returning "?" for unrecognized values.
Maps a GroupState enum value to its lowercase display string ("hostile", "engaged", or "peaceful"), falling back to "?" for unrecognized values.
Maps the TownSection enum value to its display name string ("Store", "Confinement", "Morgue", "Guild", "Bank"), falling back to "?" for unknown values.
Maps a Facing enum value (N, E, S, W) to its single-letter string label, returning "?" for anything unrecognized.
Maps the EdgeClass enum value of a dungeon edge (wall, door, secret door, or open) to its display string, falling back to "?" for unknown values.
Maps a facing-relative direction index (0 to 3) to the word the player sees for it: ahead, right, behind, or left.
Maps a stat index (0–5) to its three-letter abbreviation (STR, INT, WIS, CON, CHA, or DEX as the fallback).
Converts a player's facing direction (N, E, S, W) into the grid step (dx, dy) the party moves one square in when it advances that way.
Finds and returns the stored floor whose dungeon level matches the party's current dungeon level, or nullptr if no such floor exists.
Looks up the map square at 1-based coordinates (x, y) on a dungeon floor, returning nullptr when the coordinates fall outside the 30-wide grid or past the stored squares.
Renders the party roster as text for the player, listing each member's number, name, race, active guild and level, HP and SP, status, experience and gold.
Renders the party's automap as a text grid centered on the party, showing explored squares, walls, secret doors, and doors around them, with the party marked and its facing shown as an arrow.
Returns the raw Experience Penalty (EP, rule R21) from the guild's `expFactor` field, though its header marks it as a placeholder that should return 0 until reconciled, which the code does not do.

Returns the race's experience modifier (RACE_MOD, R21) used in level-up experience calculations, currently passing through the stored integer expFactor unchanged rather than the neutral 1.0 the header comment describes.

Returns the guild's raw Gold Parameter (goldFactor) from the guild data, but is a placeholder that returns that field directly until the assumed field names are reconciled with the generated game_data.h.
Placeholder for the spell rate lookup (SpellDef::rate[k], rule R29) that always returns a neutral 1.0 until the field is reconciled with the generated game data.
Placeholder for the spell-max-per-level lookup (R29) that always returns 0, so no spell is castable until the real SpellDef member is wired in.
Re-acquaints a character with a guild they have already joined by making it their active guild, returning false if they never joined it (free of cost, per R13.1).
Returns false if any worn item is cursed, so a character wearing cursed gear is refused when trying to join a guild (SRD R13.4).
Decides whether a character may join a guild by checking that no entry in the guild's unmet requirements list remains, so the join is refused if any requirement is unmet.
Decides how a character's eligibility for a guild is shown during creation: hidden if the race is not allowed, italic if the alignment is not allowed, bold if the stats qualify, and plain otherwise.
Appends a guild log entry (stamped with the current game day, guild, kind, and text) to the game state's guild log and emits a "guild.log.added" message to the context.
Forwards to setActiveGuild while ignoring the inventory and town arguments, since the wiki gate from R18 was not implemented in the engine excerpt, so no guild-change restriction is applied.

Runs the guild hall's Make Level procedure: it checks guild membership, max level, experience, and quest completion, takes the gold fee, then applies the level gain, title, mastership, new quest, and hit increase.
Computes the experience points required to reach a given level, combining the guild's experience penalty and the race's experience modifier with the 1995 Mordor level-curve formula (R21).
Converts an experience point total into an actual EP value for the Mordor rules by dividing it by 8 (R24).
Converts a character's Gold Parameter (GP) into an actual gold modifier using the formula GP/10 + 1 (rule R24 of the Mordor SRD).
Computes the gold a character must have to reach a given guild level, using the wiki's formula with the guild's raw Gold Parameter as the multiplier.

Computes the gold a character needs to advance from a given level, summing a per-level cost that grows with level and scaling the total by the guild's gold parameter, using the 1995 game's rounding rules.

Decides whether a character can cast a given spell in a guild, comparing the spell's level and the guild's spell maximum against the member's guild level, and computes the spell level shown to the player (floored from level times rate).
Finds the best ability chance across the character's joined guilds, returning the highest per-guild chance for the given ability (per the Mordor guild rules R34.2/R35).
Always returns 0 with its argument ignored, as a placeholder because MonsterDef has no monsterClass field yet.
Returns a monster's floor by reading its levelFound field, standing in for a floor value that the game data does not define on MonsterDef.
Ignores its monster argument and always returns kRareMonsterWeight as the monster's rarity, because the rarity field isn't confirmed in game_data.h, so no monster is ever rejected as rare.
Always returns 0 with its GuildDef argument ignored, because the guild forfeit cost field is not yet defined in game_data.h, so no levels are dropped when a quest is forfeited.
Reports whether a guild definition is the Nomad guild, going by its data name "Nomad".
Converts a non-negative integer to its decimal text representation, used to format day gaps in log prefixes.
Returns the remainder of a divided by b, or 1 when b is zero, as a plain arithmetic helper with no game meaning (the zero case is an unresolved guess, not a rule).
Scans the item definition table and returns the index of the first item whose type matches the given kind, or -1 if none does.
Returns the index of the first monster whose class matches the given class id, or 0 if no monster has that class.
Scans the monster table in order and returns the index of the first monster whose levelFound is at least the given tier, or -1 if none qualifies.
Finds the index of the last monster in the monster table whose floor is at or above the given tier, which is the boundary used to limit a quest's monster selection by depth, per SRD rule R51.

Computes a character's Adventure Difficulty (A/D) gain interval at a given level for a guild, using the hits-cap level, the guild's AdEvery and AdMaxLevel values, and a +3 bonus for Nomad characters, following the SRD rules R38 and R69.
Returns a constant 0 for base attack/defense without applying any formula, with the body marked UNKNOWN and the parameters explicitly voided.
Returns the Nomad guild's value for a given level, which is 10 at level 1, 10 + 1.5×level for even levels 2 through 30, and 0 for all other levels.
Resets a guild member's quest by clearing its kind and target and marking the quest as not done, as step 1 of the R42 quest-forfeit or reassignment procedure.
At a new guild level, it rolls whether the player gets a quest (or is let off), then assigns a defeat-monster or fetch-item target scaled to the quest tier.
Computes the maximum monster level a guild's quests can reach, which is its guild level divided by 25 (rounded down) and capped at 10, per rule R48.
Computes the maximum item level allowed for a guild's quest reward, derived from the quest monster level for the guild's level and capped at a fixed maximum.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.QuestItemBand (paired with Rules.QuestTier for the first step)

what: On arrival in town, guild-marked items in pack slots 1 through 39 have their charges restored to their maximum (guild item recharge, rules R62 and R63).

Sets a companion's Hits field to the given value, doing nothing with the context; the header comment says the R67 rule concerns fn1163 writing Hits rather than Name, but this function itself only copies a number into a struct field.

Computes the hit points a character gains when reaching a new guild level, using the guild's average hits, a 2/3 chance of a random bonus, a Constitution bonus above 16, and a cap of 999 maximum hits.

When a character is a member of a guild, this checks whether they can claim the guildmaster seat, and if the claim succeeds, places the guild crest in their pack and tells the player whether it was placed, there was no room, or they already hold it.
Maps a character's alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil) to its corresponding guild-mask bit, which is used when checking guild membership eligibility by alignment.
Counts how many of a guild's extra-swing level thresholds a character of the given level has reached, returning the number of additional swings for Multiple Swings guilds and 0 for all others.

Rolls the hit points a character gains on reaching the next level in a guild, using the guild's average hits, a 2/3 chance of a random bonus, and a CON-based bonus below the hit-cap level, or a flat late-hits amount past that cap.

Computes the attack and defence bonuses a character gains on reaching a given level for a guild, using a placeholder linear interpolation from zero up to the guild's maximum at the maximum level, rather than the real SRD per-level rule.
Returns a guild's maximum Attack and Defence values by looking them up in per-guild tables, which the header notes are maxed independently and follow the character sheet for Sorcerer and Wizard.
Computes a character's attack and defence caps in Mordor by taking the per-field maximum of the attack and defence limits of every guild the character has joined.
Computes nothing and returns a fixed 0 for the join cost of a guild, standing in for the Mordor SRD formula that was not supplied.

Checks whether a character may join a guild, refusing if they are already a member and otherwise testing race, alignment, minimum stats, and gold on hand, and sends the player a refusal message when already joined.

Makes a character advance a guild level by checking membership, experience and gold, charging the advance cost, adding hits and new attack/defence values, clearing an item quest, and refusing with a message when any requirement is unmet.
Item (fetch) quests can only be started by the player once their guild level exceeds kItemQuestMinGuildLevel (15), a gate the engine enforces in place of the wiki's "begins at level 15" rule.
Decides whether a monster of a given floor is eligible for a quest, where the quest tier is capped at kQuestTierMax (10) and the monster qualifies if its floor is no deeper than that capped tier.
Computes the index range for an item pick (first+1 through last), collapsing to a single index when the span is zero, with no game-rule decision beyond the index arithmetic.

Checks whether a character who has joined a guild outranks the current guildmaster, and if so installs the character as the new guildmaster (taking the master's level and name, and recording the roster index when the character is in the roster) and announces the claim to the player.
Returns the title string from the first band in a level-indexed table whose upper bound exceeds the given level, or an empty string if none match.
Checks whether a guild index falls within the valid range of guilds (0 up to kGuildCount), which the guild rules rely on before looking up or assigning a guild.
Returns the maximum character level for the Nomad, Sorcerer, and Wizard guilds (30, 29, and 41 respectively), with 0 for all other guilds as an unknown placeholder.
Returns a constant 0 for the hits-gain-below-ML value of any guild, ignoring its argument, as a placeholder because the SRD excerpt does not give that data.
Returns a constant 0 for the guild's hits-gain threshold (MH) as a placeholder, since the per-guild value is not in the source excerpt.
Returns the cost to join a guild, which the engine sets to 0 whether or not the character already holds another guild, since the priced amount for an extra guild is not given in the source.
Always returns false, reporting that the character has no cursed worn gear, because the cursed flags for worn items live in Inventory and cannot be read from Character here.
Lets a character who has already joined a guild make it their active guild again, failing if the guild ID is invalid or the character has not joined it.

Reports whether a character has joined a given guild, returning false for an invalid guild index and otherwise reading the character's "joined" flag, which serves as the availability test for guild-related level content in the game's rules.

Decides whether a character who has joined a guild may be re-offered the sitting guildmaster position, which happens only when the character's level is strictly above the level recorded for the current master and the character's name matches the holder.
Computes a guild's quest tier from its level by dividing by 25, rounding half-to-even, and clamping the result between 1 and the quest tier cap (kQuestTierCap).
Returns true when the rounded draw is at most kLetOffMaxRoll, which is the let-off check in AssignQuest that grants the quest let-off chance (about 5.5% per the engine's stated value).
Decides whether a rare monster (weight ≤ 9) or rare item (weight ≤ 4) pick should be rerolled, with a 75% chance of rejecting it; non-rare entries are never rejected.
Decides whether the item fetch quest is offered to a guild member, which happens only when the guild level is above the threshold kItemFetchMinGuildLevel (15, per the c19 source).
Returns a random integer in the half-open range first+1 through last (or first+1 when the span is zero or negative), using the context's RNG.
Rolls a quest for a joined guild member at their current level, either letting them off with no task or assigning them a Defeat or Fetch quest at a level tier, and announces the result to the player.

Forfeits a player character's membership in a guild by clearing its experience and quest progress, marking it unjoined, reverting the active guild to Nomad if it was the one left, and posting a "You have left the guild" message.
Computes a character's guild-based attack and defense awards as the highest att and highest def across all guilds the character has joined, taking each stat's maximum independently.
Produces the Char-page attack and defense values for a character by taking the raw best guild award and adding the base 10/10 AD, per the game's rules.

Computes the hit points a guild member gains on level-up or advance: the fixed maximum-hits value at or above the guild's max level, otherwise a base increment plus a 2/3-chance random bonus and the Constitution bonus.
Rolls a random bonus of 1 to (CON − 16) hit points when a character's Constitution is above 16, and returns 0 otherwise.
Returns a hand width for an item, currently a hardcoded fallback of 1 because the real value lives in item data that isn't available.

Returns the Table T-2 wear class cap for an item, which is meant to limit which classes may wear it (0 means unwearable, a positive number is the maximum, -1 means no cap), but it currently always returns the no-cap value because the data field is not yet wired.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.MaxWornOfClass (used with Character.WearClassOf to go from item to class)

what: Returns a constant 0 for an item's stat requirement because the item-data field is not available, so it always reports that no requirement exists.
Checks whether a slot number falls within the range of valid item equipment slots, which is a gate on whether an item can be equipped to or removed from a slot.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs is.CanUnequip (the candidate's name is garbled in the list, so this is the closest match I can see)

what: Returns true if the character has joined any guild, checking each guild slot in turn, which the equipment check uses as a gate on equipping items.
Shows the player the refusal message for an equip attempt that failed, mapping each refusal outcome (no free hands, too many worn, class or guild restriction, stats too low) to its text.
Returns true when the given internal item-slot index is the Hands slot (index 0), which the SRD defines as the hands equipment slot.
Reports whether an inventory item slot is empty, using the placeholder rule that an item with id 0 counts as empty, since the SRD Formulas section defining slot emptiness was not supplied.
Checks whether the hands the player is already using, plus the item's hand width, stay within the two-hand limit (R6), so an item can be equipped only if enough hands are free.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.EquipProblem (with Character.HandsUsed as the running hand count)

what: Checks whether an item can be equipped under its wear-class limit: unwearable items are refused, and an item is refused when the player already has that class's maximum number of items equipped.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.EquipProblem (with Character.IsWearable covering the cap-0 refusal)

what: Checks whether a character meets every stat requirement for an item, returning false if any current stat falls below the item's required value for that stat.
Equips a pack item for a character if the equip check passes, marking it equipped, reducing free hands by the item's hand width, and applying any equip curse tied to the character's alignment.
Returns whether a worn item's slot may be unequipped, which it may not while the slot's curse flag is set (rule R13).

Unequips a worn item from an inventory slot, refusing if the slot is empty, not an item slot, or flagged as cursed, otherwise clearing the item's equipped state and releasing its hand width back to the free hands.
stageB_where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.Mdi.cs, EquipSelected (the "on.EquipSelected" header in the candidate list)

what: At item generation, it marks the item's slot as cursed when the item is a Cursed==2 type or the item came from chest treasure landing in a pack slot.
When a slot is unequipped, its curse flag is cleared, so the curse comes back the next time the item is equipped.
Computes the worth of an attack or defence (AD) value after alignment fit: full value is kept, adjacent alignment halves it with round-half-even rounding, and opposed alignment negates it.

Converts a raw item alignment value from the item data into the game's alignment category (Unaligned, Good, Neutral, or Evil), treating values 0 and 1 as Unaligned and falling back to Unaligned for out-of-range values.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Import/OriginalSaves.cs SlotFrom (containing class not shown in the candidate)

what: When a character picks up an item, it raises the item's identification level to the level the reader can achieve, never lowering it.
Reports whether a character is incapacitated, which in this implementation means dead or paralysed, so they cannot use items; the SRD does not define the condition, so this is a chosen behaviour.

Applies the item-use rules for Mordor in a fixed order: it refuses silently if the user is incapacitated or the item's special type is negative, reports "no effect", "out of charges", "must be in the dungeon", "Nothing Happens" or "must be equipped" as appropriate, and computes the item's alignment fit against the user before the charge is spent.

Decides whether a spell on an item fires when used by a character, succeeding if the item is unaligned or its alignment exactly matches the user's alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil), with no partial-strength case.
Does nothing: it takes the context, user, item and fit class, discards them all, and leaves a comment saying the half, subtract and full cases are handled elsewhere or not at all.
Reduces the character's age by the requested number of years (365 days each), clamping it at a minimum of 16 years and emitting a "You cannot get any younger." message when the floor is hit.
Applies a stat modifier to a character by delegating to the shared stat-modification rule (applyStatMod in items1b), with the reversed flag controlling whether positive modifiers are inverted.

Swaps two item slots in the player's pack (and their spell-buffer references) after checking that both slot indices are valid and distinct, with no game rule applied beyond the drag UI's arrangement of items.
When an inventory slot is emptied, this resets every spell buffer that points to that slot back to the empty marker (-1), so the character no longer casts from a slot that has been cleared.
Walks the character's spell-buffer slot list and swaps any entry pointing at slot A with slot B (and vice versa), so buffers follow the item when two inventory slots are swapped by dragging.

When a character is given an item, giveRead raises the item's identification level to whatever level the receiver can read from it, if that is higher than the current level, and announces the identification to the party.
Attempts a shop purchase by placing the item in the buyer's first free inventory slot if one exists and the buyer has enough gold, deducting the price and reporting the result to the player.
Returns the realignment cost multiplier for changing an item's alignment in the game: 0 for the same alignment, 1 for a neighbouring step, and 2 for anything further across the spectrum.
Uncurses an equipped cursed item in the player's pack by clearing its curse flag, refusing with a message if the item is not cursed or not equipped.

Returns true when an item's id falls within the guild crest id range, treating crests as items with ids between kCrestItemIdBase (exclusive) and kCrestItemIdBase + kGuildCount (inclusive), though the actual crest identification rule is unknown and not specified in this SRD half.
Quotes a sell price for an item, refusing guild crests outright (returning false) before any price is computed.
Parses a typed gold amount string (optional spaces, sign, and up to four decimal places) into an integer count of 1/10000 gold, rejecting empty, non-numeric, zero, or overly large input.
Decides whether a bank deposit is permitted by checking that the requested gold amount is positive and does not exceed the gold the player is carrying.
Decides whether a bank withdrawal of the given amount is allowed, refusing it when the amount exceeds the gold held in the bank or the bank balance is negative.
Always returns false, ignoring its arguments, as a placeholder because the bank retrieval re-identification formula (R66) is missing from this SRD half.
Rolls a d100 and reports whether the roll is at or below 50 plus twice the dungeon level, which decides whether a slime attack reaches the player.
Returns a random integer slot number from 1 to 39 using the game's RNG, with no game rule applied beyond the draw itself.
Returns the display name of an item's definition looked up by its id from the game data, or "Unidentified Item" when the id is out of range.
Returns the name of the item type at the given index in the item-type table, or "Unidentified Item" if the index is out of range.
Decides whether an item is destructible by a monster or slime, returning true unless its special type falls in the guild-marker range (below 500 or above the destructible maximum of 511).
Clears one pack slot of an inventory by resetting it to an empty item and writes a "<prefix><Name> Destroyed!" message naming the item's base name.
Rolls a placeholder 50 percent chance, when a monster hits the player, to destroy a destructible item in the given pack slot if its level qualifies, and removes it if the roll succeeds.
Decides whether a theft against a monster succeeds, using a percent chance equal to the thief's score minus twice the monster's level, clamped to 0–100.
When the quicksand hazard (R73) fires, it picks a random item slot from 1 to 39 and reports the quicksand message if that slot holds an item, though the outcome itself is left unimplemented.

Decides whether a Seer carrier's item is hit by a given effect: named items always hit, and other items hit only if their type code is valid and their drop level falls within the floor up to floor plus a random band of 0 to kSeerBandSides-1.
Rolls a uniform random number of take carriers from 1 to kSeerTakeMax for the Seer's take effect, a stand-in until the real take formula from the Formulas table is available.

Returns the combined effect bits of all equipped items that apply under the fit rules (Table T-5), delegating the actual calculation to gearEffects, with Critical Hit and Backstab excluded from having any effect.
Returns a placeholder price of zero currency, rounded half-even, with no game-specific logic behind it.
Returns the buy price of an item for the default case of one copy on the shelf, delegating the actual price calculation to storeBuyPrice.
Computes the gold fee to uncurse an item by looking up its list price in the item data and applying the SRD's uncurse-fee formula, returning 0 if the item isn't found.
Clamps an integer value to the inclusive range [lo, hi], returning lo if it is below the range, hi if above it, and the value itself otherwise.
Returns true when an item-pack slot index is greater than zero and below the pack's slot count (kPackSlots), so it checks that an index falls inside the pack's valid range.
Looks up an item definition by its numeric id, returning a pointer into the game's item table, or null if the id is zero, negative, or out of range.
Looks up a character's race definition from the game data by the race's numeric index, returning a pointer to that entry or null if the index is out of range.
Returns the display name of an item by looking up its definition from the item's id, or an empty string if no definition exists.
Reports whether an item was issued by a guild, which the game uses to decide whether it can be dropped, given, or swapped.
Returns the item-use multiplier for a guild, giving Nomads and Healers their own factors and 1.0 for every other guild.
Checks whether a given guild is allowed to use an item by testing the bit for that guild in the item's guilds mask.
Checks whether a character's membership in guild g is active, meaning joined with a level above zero, and for class-restricted items that guild must also be the character's primary (active) guild.
Computes the guild-use level a player needs to use an item, as a real number: the item's level-scale factor multiplied by a guild-dependent factor (plus 2.97 times that factor), with a floor of 1.0.
Returns true if any guild that the character belongs to (within the class-restriction scope) is on the item's guild-allowed mask, which is the "can use" check for guild-restricted items.
Returns true if any guild the character belongs to, in scope for the item's class restriction, has a level at or above the level that guild requires to use the item.
Maps a SwapResult code to its matching fixed user-facing error string (guild-issued or equipped/banked source or destination), returning an empty string for any other value.
Maps an item alignment value (good, neutral, evil) to its short display tag " (g)", " (n)", " (e)", or an empty string.
Decides whether two item alignments can be combined, returning true when they match or either item is Unaligned, a rule the SRD does not specify and this code marks as an assumption.

Maps a CombineCheck result code to the fixed explanatory suffix string shown when two items cannot be combined (wrong class, different type, or incompatible alignment), returning an empty string otherwise.
Applies the stat modifiers from an item definition to a character's stats, one stat at a time, optionally in reverse (for example, when the item is removed), as a special effect of the item.
Rolls a d100 for a slime attack, returning a value from 1 to 100 that is compared against the hit threshold (50 + dungeon level × 2) to decide whether the slime hits.
Decides whether a slime attack hits by comparing a roll against a base value plus a bonus that scales with dungeon level.
Equips a pack item for the character if it's a valid, non-refused item, setting its equipped flag and applying any alignment-based curse via fitFor.
Checks whether a cursed item can be uncursed by returning NotCursed if the item isn't cursed, NotEquipped if it isn't equipped, otherwise Ok, following the game's uncurse ordering.
Attempts to remove a curse from an equipped item, reporting "not cursed" or "not equipped" to the player when the uncurse is refused, and otherwise clearing the item's curse flag.
Forces a worn item off the character when it has an equip problem (such as a class or alignment restriction) and the item is not cursed, so the item is unequipped.
Checks whether an item can be given to another character, refusing if it is guild-issued, currently equipped, or the recipient has no free inventory slot, in that order.
Moves an item from one inventory's pack slot into the first free slot of another inventory, refusing and posting a player message if the item is guild-issued, equipped, or the destination is full.
Returns whether an item can be deposited in the vault, which it cannot if it is currently equipped (rule T-10).
Makes a bank deposit by moving gold from the character's on-hand purse into the bank balance, returning Beep if the amount is non-positive or exceeds the gold on hand.
Withdraws gold from the party's bank account into hand, failing with a Beep result if the requested amount exceeds the bank balance or the bank balance is negative.

Decides whether an item should be re-identified when retrieved, returning true when the probe roll exceeds the threshold (the port's chosen reading of the SRD rule, which says re-identify when the probe is below the threshold).
Attempts to buy an item by finding a free inventory slot and checking the buyer has enough gold, then deducting the price and placing the item in the pack, returning Ok, NoFreeSlot, or NotEnoughGold.

Checks whether two inventory slots can be swapped, returning OutOfRange for invalid indices, then SourceGuildIssued, DestGuildIssued, SourceEquippedOrBanked, DestEquippedOrBanked in that order, or Ok if the swap is allowed.
Swaps two player inventory slots (numbered 2 to 40) and, when requested, retargets the character's spell buffers so they keep following the moved items.
Decides whether a slime attack has any effect by comparing a slime roll against a threshold of 50 plus twice the dungeon level, so deeper levels make slime strikes more likely to hit.
Returns a random slot number from 1 to kSlimeSlotDraw by adding 1 to a bounded RNG draw, with no game-rule logic applied inside the function itself.

Rolls a random theft slot by drawing from 2 to 40 (one draw of 39 values offset by 2) to pick which item slot a thief takes from.
Halves an integer with round-half-to-even rounding (so 5 becomes 2 and 7 becomes 4), returning the result as an integer, with no game-specific meaning beyond the comment's label.
Decides whether an item's alignment lets its effect bit count for a character, so an unaligned item always counts and an aligned item counts only when its alignment matches the character's.

Checks whether the player may use a pack item in the dungeon, returning NotInDungeon, NoEffect, MustBeEquipped, OutOfCharges, or Ok based on the item's special type, spell, equip state, and charges.
Ages a character by the given number of years, floors the result at the minimum adult age (16 years), and tells the player "You cannot get any younger." when the floor is hit.

Rolls a percentage check against the chance of recognising an item, computed from the character's skill and whether the item is in darkness.
Rolls a percent chance, based on the identify skill and whether the item is in fog, to decide whether an unidentified item gets renamed.
Computes how many items a seer takes from a stack of n, as a randomized rounded fraction of n clamped to between 1 and the seer maximum (3) and to n itself.
Returns nullptr unconditionally, disabling the lock-opening spell lookup because the ItemDef lockSpell field is not yet defined, with the original logic kept only in comments.
Returns whether an item can be realigned, which is refused while the item is currently equipped (rule T-11, citing SRD c22).
Appends a base-10 integer, with a leading minus sign for negatives, to a string buffer without using std::to_string.
Returns the fixed placeholder string "Unidentified Item" for any unidentified item, without computing the vaguer description the SRD mentions.
Checks whether a pack slot index falls within the usable item range 1 through 39, returning true or false.
Converts a 1-based player-facing pack slot number into the 0-based internal item index by subtracting one.
Converts a zero-based pack index into a one-based player slot number by adding one, with no game meaning of its own.
Reports whether an item's type code is 0, which the game treats as the Hands slot type.
Decides whether an item of the given type must be equipped before its spell can be used, returning true for types 1–22 and 29, 32, 33, and 34.

Decides whether a character's wear-class limit blocks equipping another item of that class: no limit (-1) never blocks, a limit of 0 always blocks, and a positive limit blocks once the number already worn reaches it.
Reports whether a special item type (stat modifiers, Potion of Youth, or Dragon's Blood) grants stat modifiers when used.
Returns the spell points a player gains from using a Scroll of Spells (50) or Tome of Spells (200), and 0 for any other special item type.

Returns the age change in days that a special item type applies to a character: the Potion of Youth makes them 365 days younger, Dragon's Blood makes them 3650 days younger, and special type 25 gives +28 days (sign and magnitude marked unknown in the source), with 0 for any other type.
Returns true when a special item type value falls in the guild crest range (500 through 500 + kGuildCount − 1), marking the item as a crest belonging to one of the game's guilds.
Returns the crest marker id for a guild by adding the guild's index to a fixed base constant, with no game rule applied.

Computes how well an item's alignment fits a character's alignment, returning Full for unaligned items or matching alignments, Half for one step apart, and Subtract for two steps apart (Good versus Evil).

Returns true only when an item's fit to a character is a full match (FitClass::Full), which is the condition for the item's effect bits to count, while opposed-fit curses are handled separately by applyEquipCurse.

Maps the original game's identification code (0 through 3, counting down from All to Barely) to the matching identification level, or Unknown for any other code, which governs how well the player can identify an item.
Returns the item-use factor for a guild, with Nomad at 0.8 and Healer at 1.5 and 1.0 as a placeholder default for the other guilds whose values are unknown.
Computes the minimum character level needed to use a guild item, as (use factor + use factor × 2.97) × level scale, floored at 1.
Clamps a raw item chance value (for Identify, Recognise, Rename, or Destroy) to the minimum and maximum bounds defined for that chance kind.
Rolls d100 and returns true when the roll is below 50 + 2 × dungeon level, deciding whether the slime effect takes hold on the player.
Rolls a random seer band from 0 to 2 for the game's seer mechanic, using the context's RNG.
Clamps a seer's carrier count to between 1 and kSeerMaxCarriers, so the seer-related game mechanic never uses a count outside the allowed range.

Reports whether a change of alignment, going from one alignment index to another, crosses more than one step on the alignment spectrum, using the raw index difference.
Parses a numeric value (optional sign, integer and fractional digits, leading spaces skipped) from a substring of a string, returning whether any digits were found and the parsed double.

Returns true when an item's id is zero, which the code treats as the encoding for an empty inventory slot (the comment flags this encoding as unconfirmed).
Returns the receiver's item's current idLevel unchanged, ignoring the context and receiver, because the knowledge re-read formula is not yet implemented.
Maps a character's library identification level (all or mostly identified) to the corresponding library grade value (4, 3, or 0 otherwise).

Dropping a dragged item slot onto a spell buffer clears that buffer on the character's order (if the index is valid) and reports that the buffer was emptied.
Moves a dragged pack slot into the first empty vault slot, refusing hands, guild-issued items, and equipped items, and reporting "Out of room!" when the vault is full.
Blocks equipping and dropping pack items for any character whose paralysed ailment is set, per the game's paralysis rule.

Checks that an item pack slot index is within the valid range, from 1 up to kLastPackIndex.

Returns a constant 0 currency for any sale, with a comment noting the store sale formula is not yet known.

Decides whether a store will accept (shelve) an item for sale, letting unaligned items through and otherwise requiring the item's alignment to match the store's alignment, using an assumed rule the comment marks as unconfirmed.
Reports whether an item is part-used, meaning its current charges are below the item's maximum charges (rule R61), which requires maxCharges to be positive.
Returns true when an item is not fully identified (idLevel is not All), so the identify fee applies only to items whose properties are not yet fully known.

Identifies an item for a Character payer by charging an identify fee from their purse (refusing if they can't afford it or the item is empty or already identified) and then raising the item's identification level to full.

Realigns a companion to a chosen alignment if it is offered as an option and the payer can afford the realignment price, deducting that price from the payer's purse.
Returns a constant 0 for the sell price of a companion, ignoring all its arguments, as a placeholder until the sell price table is available.

Swaps the contents of two pack slots in the exchange window, refusing out-of-range or hand-slot moves (with a "Sorry!" message for out-of-range) and reporting the outcome.
Returns true when the number of worn items of a class is below the wear cap, so another item of that class may be worn.

Looks up the spell attached to an item by its 1-based spell index, returning the zero-based index into the spell list, or -1 if the item has no valid spell.
Returns the spell level at which an item's magical spell is cast, computed from the item's level and the user's spell level via casting3's itemSpellLevel formula.
Decides whether casting a level-0 item spell costs spell points, which it does unless the p01AA flag is set, and treats any higher-level cast as free.
Computes the store's fee for an item from its price by multiplying by 0.8, dividing by 0.5, and rounding half-to-even, per SRD chapter 13's item and equipment rules.
Returns true when the shelf is on floor 0 and has at least one unaligned item stocked, which decides whether the shop sells unaligned goods at the item's price.

Sells an inventory item to the store for its computed price, adding the gold to the character's wallet and clearing the slot, or refuses the sale with a result code if the slot is empty or the gold total would overflow.

Always returns 0 with an empty body, so it does not compute any times-cast count for the item (the function is a placeholder).

Picks one item category (or a fixed item ID) at random from a drop table row by rolling a random slot index and decoding the stored value, with no direct game effect of its own.
Builds the list of item IDs eligible to appear for a given level range and item category, taking one contiguous run of matching items starting at the first match, per SRD rule R7.

Advances an item's identification level by one step per Identify click, with the General Store allowed to reach the full level and other locations capped at the level just below it.

Works out the identification level a recipient achieves when exchanging an item, applying the R13 quirk where the item's levelScale names another item whose difficulty values set the result, and never returning a level below the item's current idLevel.

Spends one charge from a charge item (cost-free to the user, so long as charges remain) and reports the spell it casts at its fixed level, leaving the actual spell effect to the caller; if no charges remain, the cast fails.
Adds the item's spell-point bonus to the user's current spell points on use (e.g. Scroll of Spells +50, Tome of Spells +200) and announces the restored amount to the player, with no cap applied.
When a character equips or unequips an item, its stat modifiers are added to or removed from the character's ability stat modifiers, and a message is shown.
Computes a character's thieving ability as a 0-100 score from Dex, Wis, guild level and thieving modifier, normalized against a baseline and maximum (formula F6 / rule R18 of the Mordor SRD).
Returns the number of item templates in the static game data by taking the size of the items container, for use in bounds checks.
Returns true when the given item id is a valid index into the game data's item table, i.e. it is non-negative and below the item count.

Looks up the author's minimum item level for a given drop level (1-16), clamping out-of-range values, which determines the lowest level an item can be generated at when dropped.

Given a character's identification skill, the item's difficulty, and the dungeon level, it determines how well the item is identified (Mostly, Partial, or Barely), with shallow-level items fully Mostly-identified when skill meets difficulty.

Parses a JSON text string into a JsonValue, rejecting it with an error message if parsing fails or if non-whitespace characters remain after the top-level value.

Scans the game data's item list in order and returns the index of the first item whose type matches the given type and whose floor is at least the given minimum, or -1 if none does.
Returns a reference to the party member at the given index, a plain container accessor with no game rule applied.
Returns a const reference to the party member at the given index, converting the signed index to an unsigned one for the array access, with no game rule applied.
Returns a reference to the party's per-member inventory array (`party.inventories`), a plain container accessor with no game rule applied.
Scans the pack-slot array of an inventory and returns the index of the first slot whose id is zero, or -1 if no slot is free.
Decrements the per-alignment count on a shelf by one for the given alignment, ignoring the item id.

Checks whether a given chest trap (such as Not Trapped through Withering) is set in a bitmask of trap flags for a chest in the game.

Placeholder for rolling chest items by dungeon level and chest class; it ignores all its arguments and appends nothing to the output list, since the item band table is not yet supplied.

Applies damage to a trap's hit count, leaving the remaining hits after the damage with a floor of zero.

Picks which party member receives a share of chest gold by mapping a random roll onto a party index, with ties rounded half-to-even and the result clamped to valid range.

Splits a chest's gold equally among the living party members, gives any remainder to a chosen receiver (or the first living member if that receiver is dead), and pays nothing if the opener was killed by the trap.
Splits a chest's gold pot evenly among a number of shares, with integer division that discards any remainder and returns zero when there are no valid shares.
Reports whether an item is cursed for the purposes of a slot, returning true when the item's curse value is anything other than none (kind 1 and kind 2 curses are not distinguished).
Rolls a random amount of gold between zero and the victim's whole purse for a thief's take, capping the result at the purse total.
Returns true when the sum of a character's gold on hand and gold in the bank is at least the given price, so a purchase can be covered from combined funds.
Deposits gold from the player's carried purse into their bank balance, refusing amounts that are zero, negative, or more than the gold on hand.

Lets a player withdraw gold from their bank balance into their on-hand purse, refusing only when the requested amount exceeds what the bank holds (negative amounts are accepted per the CONFLICT-10 port rule).

Assigns a guild quest by clearing the membership's quest to an empty GuildQuest (kind None) and recording the guild level, since the quest kinds, targets and counts are not defined in the source text.
Placeholder that accepts its arguments, ignores them, and adds no monster drops, since the monster drop tables and laired bonus are not in the provided SRD text.
Converts a character's Known (identification) value, clamped to the valid scale, into an IdLevel, where values at or below zero mean the item is fully identified.

Removes one randomly drawn item from a shop's stock as a buy-out, making up to maxDraws random picks (unbounded if negative) and accepting the first draw, since the acceptance test is not yet specified.
Scans one member's pack slots in order and copies the given item into the first slot whose id is zero or negative, clearing its equipped flag, returning whether a free slot was found.
Places an item into the first free pack slot found by trying each party member in turn from a random starting member, returning whether any slot was found, with no game message on failure.

Computes a monster's overall power rating from its attack, strength, hit points, dexterity, and guild level, plus bonuses for each special attack and spell flag it has.

Decides whether a party member falls down a chute, which happens unless the character is levitating and the rules say they hover over the pit at this dungeon level.
Computes the chute-fall landing damage, returning 0 if the character is Levitating and otherwise the standard chute damage for the landing level and race size.
Moves a character who fell down a chute to the landing floor, keeping their X and Y position and setting their area to the one at that spot on the lower floor.
Announces to the player that a character has fallen through a chute and then been hurt by the landing, showing the damage taken.

Multiplies two 1995 Mordor x87 extended-precision values, rounding the 64-bit mantissa product half to even, with zero short-circuiting to zero.

Returns true when a quest item's spawn weight is at or below the threshold kQuestRareItemMaxWeight (4), marking that item as rare under rule R34.
Rolls a percent chance (74%, per the R34 comment) that a rare quest entry gets rerolled.
Decides whether an item is excluded from quest-item assignment, rejecting cursed items, items of level 0, and items worth less than the minimum quest value (100 gold).

Returns the element count of a generic vector as a 32-bit integer, with no game meaning.

Compares a string to a C string literal ignoring ASCII case, returning true only if every character matches and the lengths are equal.

Returns true if any character in the string `s` appears anywhere in the character set `set`, otherwise false.

Returns true when a character is a JSON whitespace character (space, tab, carriage return, or newline), with no game meaning.

Scans a fixed table of manifest field names for a case-insensitive match against the given key and returns the matching index, or -1 if none matches.

Copies one of eight string values into the matching named field of a mod manifest (id, name, version, author, game version, assembly, entry type, or description) based on a numeric field index, ignoring any other index.
Shows the player a "mod.json could not be parsed" message and returns false to signal that the mod's manifest failed to load.
Ignores its LiveMod argument and always returns ModKind::Lifecycle, because the real kind isn't available in this file.

Parses the text of a mod.json manifest into a ModManifest struct, reporting an event and returning false if the text is empty or malformed, though the function is truncated before its final return.

Checks a mod's manifest against the chapter 21 validation rule (F1), returning the first problem found: a blank id, an id containing forbidden characters, a blank assembly, or a blank entry type, or None if the manifest is valid.
Maps a manifest-validation problem code to its fixed human-readable error message string, returning an empty string for no problem.
Reports whether a mod id is already taken in the host's mod list, so a later mod with the same id is skipped and the first one found is kept (rule R5).
Scans the host's mod list for an entry whose id exactly matches the given string and returns its index, or -1 if none matches.
Builds a LiveMod's display title from its manifest, using the mod's name (or id when the name is blank) followed by its version if one is set, per formula F2 of chapter 21.
Returns true if a text string is empty or contains only whitespace characters, with no game meaning.
Reports whether a mod is enabled for a given mod id by reading that mod's stored "Enabled" flag from the settings store, defaulting to disabled when no value is stored.
Records the mod's "Enabled" flag (true or false) into the mod settings store for the given mod ID.
At startup, it walks the discovered mods in order and loads and switches on each one that the player has enabled, skipping any with a manifest validation problem or a fault.

Reactivates a previously loaded mod by setting it active again, and for lifecycle-kind mods it announces that the host must call OnEnable and re-note the Harmony patches.
Deactivates a loaded mod by marking it inactive and emitting the messages telling the host to call OnDisable (for lifecycle mods) and to remove the mod's Harmony patches.

Switches a mod on or off at runtime: it saves the setting, and if the mod is a lifecycle mod that is not faulted it loads or reactivates it (or deactivates it when switched off), otherwise deferring the change to the next start or refusing a switch-on with a bad manifest.

Given a hook's status, it decides whether the original game answer is used: only an Ok status lets the mod's decision stand, while a null decision or a throw falls back to the original's answer (rule R12.3).

Applies the mod's hook reply to the game: if the hook threw, the mod is faulted for the session and the original answer is used, and if the decision was null the original's answer is kept, otherwise the mod's answer stands.

Disables a mod for the rest of the session after it faults, marking it faulted with a reason, deactivating it, and emitting events so the host removes its Harmony patches and the original rule answer is used instead.
When the mod settings store changes a setting, it raises one "setting changed" event and then forwards that event to each loaded mod whose id matches the changed mod's id.

Returns whether a named toggle is on for a loaded mod, reading the stored flag for that mod and key and falling back to the toggle's declared default when none is saved, or false if the mod index is invalid.
Looks up a toggle in a mod's manifest by its key, ignoring case, and returns that toggle's default value, or false if no toggle has that key.

Resolves a player's stored choice for a mod setting against the declared options, falling back to the default option and then the first option when the stored value does not match, per the mod-choice rule (F6).
Returns the stored true/false setting for a mod's key, falling back to the given default when nothing is stored or the stored text is neither "True" nor "False".
Stores a mod setting flag as the text "True" or "False" in the mod settings store, following the chapter 21 formula F4 for saving toggle values.
Returns the text a mod has stored under a given key for that mod, or an empty string if nothing is stored.

Declares a new mod toggle on a manifest, adding it to the declared settings unless a toggle with the same key (matched case-insensitively) already exists, in which case the existing toggle wins and the code default is ignored (R17).
Records the player's chosen text for a mod option under a given key, writing it straight into the mod settings store without checking it against the declared options.

Maps a mod API member (toggle, Has/Remove, choices, table/list settings, settings window, OptionDescriptions) to the Mordor mod API version that introduced it, returning -1 for unknown or out-of-range members.

Returns the number of entries in the game's monster table (ctx.data.monsters) as a 32-bit integer.
