Decides what happens to the party leader's saved character record when the party disbands: leave it untouched if the leader is dead, blank it if the party is solo, otherwise write or delete it depending on whether the party reloads when loaded.
stageB_where: Mordor.Mod.QoL/QolMod.cs QolMod.TownLeader (no candidate covers the disband record decision; Mordor.App/PartyUnload.cs PartyUnload.Run is the closest, since it decides what happens to the leader's record on unload)

what: When a town autoload runs, it walks the remembered party members, announces each one's outcome to the player (load error, not here, dead, opposite alignment, or joined), adds eligible members to the party, and then prunes the dead.
Returns the gold a character can spend for an exchange: only on-hand gold while in the dungeon, but on-hand plus banked gold when in town (rule R23.2).
Transfers gold from one character's exchange allowance to another (R23), rejecting zero-amount and over-limit transfers with a "Too Much!" message, and otherwise moving the gold between wallets.
Returns the index of the party member after the currently selected one, wrapping back to 0 at the end, or 0 if the party is empty.
Switches the commanded party member to the chosen index, resetting the Spell Type box, and reports whether the town shops and buildings should refresh (leader alive and not in the dungeon, per R6).
Under rule R28, Alt+1 through Alt+4 switch the active command when the party has more than one member and the chosen slot is occupied.
At room entry, when a hostile group has engaged, each party member with no combat order is given their own order as their Combat Setting, per R29.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs moves.ApplyDefaultOrders (with the per-member call to Mordor.Core/CombatOrder.cs CombatOrder.ApplyDefault)

what: Morgue Grab Body (R30.3) lets the party's selected member take up a dead character as their carry, recording the dead character's name on that member and marking the party's carrying slot as holding a dead character, with no Hide test required.
Returns the index of the first party member whose name matches the given string, or -1 if no member has that name.
Clamps the party's selected-member index so it stays within the valid range of party members, resetting it to 0 when the party is empty.
Validates that a slot index lies within the party's size and, if so, stores it as the party's selected member index, returning whether the selection succeeded.
Appends a copy of a character to the end of the party's member array, doing nothing if the party is already at its maximum size.
Removes the party member at a given index by shifting the later members left one slot, decrementing the party size, and clearing the vacated last slot; it leaves the selected-member index untouched.
Returns the area a character is saved in for game purposes, mapping dungeon level 0 (the town) to area -1 and otherwise using the character's stored area.
Applies the default combat order to a character with no order set, making them Fight, which implements the engine's default combat setting (c54).
Looks up a monster-target weight from a halving table by position, returning 0 for negative positions and for positions past the end of the table.
Sums the per-position weight from monsterTargetWeight over the first partySize party positions and returns the total, which is a helper for picking a monster's target.
Sets the party's gold leader to whichever member has the most gold in their purse, with ties going to the lowest-indexed member, and does nothing for an empty party.
Advances the party's selected-member index to the next slot, wrapping around to the first, but only when the party has more than one member, and performs no game action or UI refresh.
Maps a combat order kind (none, fight, defend, or buffer with an index) to its corresponding numeric combat-setting code, with unknown kinds falling back to "nothing."

Attempts to add a candidate character to the player's party automatically, refusing with a player-facing message if the candidate is absent, dead, the party is full, the leader is dead, or the candidate is opposite-aligned to a member, and otherwise joining them to the party.

Returns true when two alignments differ by more than kAutoloadAlignGap steps on the Good-Neutral-Evil scale, which is the rule that decides whether two party members clash enough to block autoloading.

Handles a character's attempt to join the party from the city, refusing with the matching message when the leader is dead, the party is full, the character is already in, not present, has the wrong password, or is opposed in alignment, and otherwise restoring the joiner's hit and spell points and adding them to the roster.
Checks a character's typed password against the stored one, and any character with no password set always matches.

Decides whether a dead character's body counts as lying in the city for the party's purposes: it must be dead, not the viewing character, on dungeon level 0, and not being carried by any party member.
Maps a 1-based item count to a 0-based slot index, clamping anything at or below 1 to slot 0.

Handles the player's request to remove the selected member from the party, refusing if they are the leader or monsters are nearby, asking for confirmation otherwise, and then removing them and pruning the dead.
Does nothing for a dead joiner, and otherwise just applies a default combat order to the newcomer, with its real setup body (sub0BDE, c59) absent from the source.
Refuses to set default combat orders while in combat or while monsters are in the area, and otherwise fills in the party's empty combat orders with the default.
Returns the index of the first living party member who is in the city (dungeon level 0), or -1 if no one qualifies, which determines the town gold leader per the rule c36.

Decides whether a command-switch slot number is valid for the current screen: in the dungeon it must be 1 to the party size (and party size above one), while in the city any slot from 0 upward is accepted.
Returns the smaller of two 64-bit integers, a generic math helper with no game meaning.
Clamps a raw damage value so it never exceeds the target's remaining hit points (or zero if they have none), returning the damage actually inflicted.

Computes the experience a single blow earns for the attacker or their owner, using the game's per-blow formula scaled by damage inflicted, monster and attacker guild levels, companion status, and party size.
Caps a max-hit value at the constant kHitCap (999), which is a game rule ceiling, though the function itself is a simple clamp.
Resets a character's current spell points to their maximum value, which the header's R8 step 4 describes as the per-level refill.
Recalculates a character's swings on level-up, but the body is empty (it just discards the argument) because the swing formula is not yet supplied.

Computes the award-level step for Mordor's experience progression by dividing half the experience cap plus an accuracy term by the adjusted award-level interval, rounding the result to an integer (returning 0 if the divisor is zero).
Decides whether a given character level awards an attack/defence level bonus, returning true only when the level is a positive multiple of the step and does not exceed the adMaxLevel cap.

When a character's new level qualifies as an attack/defence award level, it adds the guild's configured attack and defence increments to that character's membership in the guild and posts a message saying their attack and defence improved.
Converts a value to fixed-point form by scaling it by 10000 and rounding half-even to an integer, per SRD rule R12.

Computes the race experience multiplier f = ((ln r / ln(r+1)) + 1) − 0.7 + r/25 from the race's experience factor plus one, which scales experience awards for a character's race in the Mordor rules (SRD c05p1).
Computes the experience points a character needs to reach a given level, using the guild and race experience factors, and returns that threshold as an integer.
Rounds a double to the nearest integer with halves going up, by adding 0.5 and truncating via vbInt, with no game meaning of its own.
Computes a character's experience points needed to reach a given level in Mordor, using the R13 formula scaled by the guild's EP factor and the race factor, without rounding.
Computes a level's experience-point requirement from the R13 research formula (scaled by guild GEF and race factor), returning 0 for level 1 or below.

Computes a character's experience points required to reach a given level, scaled by a guild factor and a race experience modifier, using the SRD's closed-form XP curve (returning zero for level 1 or below).
Computes a character's experience points needed at a given level, using the wiki's level-XP formula scaled by the guild and race factors and rounded half-to-even.
Returns the XP needed to reach the next level (capped at level 998) by calling the wiki-formula XP function with the target level, guild factor, and race factor.
Computes experience points needed for a character level under the archive (c103) formula, scaling by race and guild factors and the level number, implemented literally as the source states.
Computes how much experience (XP) a character still needs to reach the total required, by subtracting current XP from the XP total.
Returns the race experience multiplier (R14 T1) for a given raw Exp value, using the tabulated values for 4 through 9, 1.0 for 3 or less, and an approximation for anything higher.
Approximates the Actual_Exp multiplier from raw experience points for R14 of the SRD, returning 1.0 for non-positive raw Exp and otherwise applying the logarithmic formula.
Returns whether a given race may take a given guild, barring Elves, Osiri, and Gnomes from Warriors and Giants, Morlochs, and Gnomes from Wizards, with every other combination allowed.
Computes the maximum stat value an item may raise a character's stat to, as the race's natural maximum for that stat plus 5.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ApplyStatMods (box.ApplyStatMods; the enclosing class name isn't shown in the candidate)

what: Converts a guild parameter value into a percentage by dividing it by the guild's divisor (kGefDivisor, 8) and multiplying by 100, per the R14 rule.
Projects a character's experience points forward to a desired level by scaling current XP by the square of the level ratio (returning 0 when the current level is invalid).
Projects a character's level from the ratio of desired to current experience points, scaled by the current level via a square root, returning 0 when current XP is non-positive.

Computes the gold cost of a level-L combat audit by summing the running total of (2i-1)×30.1 gold steps with per-step rounding, then scaling that total by a guild-gold multiplier of (1 + guildGold/10).

Computes the cumulative gold needed to reach the next character level, summing a per-level cost step (rounded half-up) for levels 1 through glvl and then scaling the total by a multiplier derived from GGF/10.
Computes the gold needed to advance from level n to n+1 under the game's R16 formula, 30.1 × n² × (1 + ggf/10), rounded half-up, where ggf is a gold-gain factor that scales the result.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.Fn12B2 (called for the current guild by Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.GoldForNextLevel)

what: Computes the total gold a character needs to advance from level 1 to level n+1 using the archive closed-form formula, scaled by a gold factor (ggf) and rounded half up.
Computes the gold needed to advance to the next level in research, as the player's gold-gain factor P (1 + GGF/10) times floor(30.1·x² + x/10), rounded half up.
Computes the gold needed to reach the next level for a character at the given level, using the wiki's formula with the gold-factor multiplier applied to the floored base amount.
Computes the gold needed to reach the next level for a character, using the wiki formula for Mordor's level-up gold requirement scaled by a gold factor, rounding the result half up.
Computes the total gold needed to reach a given level by summing the gold required for each level from 1 up to that level, scaled by a gold factor, per the wiki's R16 formula.
Computes the level a guild member falls back to when forfeiting, subtracting the cost from their current level but never dropping below level 1 (rule R17).
When a character loses levels, it reports the event and the number of levels lost, but does not change hit points because the per-level AH hit amounts are not modelled.
Reports to the player, via a message, that levels were regained below the character's maximum level, without applying the bonus hit points since their amount is not modelled.
Implements R18 of the Mordor rules: the first guild joined after Nomad costs nothing, so it returns true only when the character has not yet joined any guild besides Nomad.
Rounds a CCur value to four decimal places using round-half-even, so that a fraction like 1/3 becomes 0.3333, as the game's currency rule requires.
Checks whether at least kAilmentTickMs milliseconds have passed since the last ailment tick, so that the game's ailment effects advance every 4 seconds of real time (rule R21).

Rolls each active poison and disease against a 0-199 draw adjusted by Constitution and poison level to see whether it clears or costs hit points, and rolls an old-age check for characters at or past the onset age, then returns the hit points lost this tick.
Computes the age threshold for the old-age roll, 5 plus the natural log of how far the character's age percent exceeds the onset value (98), with a tiny floor so the log stays defined.

Arrival rest in town: moves the party to the leader's dungeon level and square, clears each member's area, rests every member (living or dead) via restInCity, reports any days passed, and returns the leader's rest days.
Rolls a percent chance, based on the character's CON, for whether a successful raise (resurrection) costs the character a point of CON.
Computes the whole seconds to add to the play clock for one step, returning zero while the game is paused and otherwise the elapsed time since the last tick, per SRD rule R27.
Returns a reference to the guild membership slot for the given guild inside a character's guild array, indexed by the guild's enum value.
Returns the guild membership record for a given guild from the character's guild list, indexing the character's guild array by the guild's numeric value.

Computes the threshold experience points needed to reach level x for a given guild and race, using a quadratic-plus-linear formula scaled by guild and race multipliers and rounded to a whole number (returning 0 for x <= 0).
Computes the party factor for experience awards, reducing the per-member share by 4% for each additional party member beyond the first (1.0 solo, 0.96 for two, 0.92 for three, 0.88 for four).
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.ExpAwarded (ChestExp in the same file uses the identical inline formula)

what: Computes the guild-level factor for a character as 333/(333+g), with negative guild levels clamped to 0, so the factor is 1.0 at guild 0 and falls toward 0 as guild level rises.

Returns the experience points needed to reach the character's current level in their guild, which is 0 at level 1 and otherwise the threshold computed by fn12A1 for the level below, based on the character's race.
Returns the highest character level among a character's other guilds (excluding the given guild), or 0 if none, which levelUp uses to apply the game's level-progression rules.
Awards experience to a character's guild membership, zeroing the award if the guild is pinned and capping the total at the guild's experience cap, then returns the amount actually banked.

Decides whether a character of a given level may receive an advancement award, which is allowed only when the level is at or below the cap and is a multiple of the award interval (the exact game meaning of these values is still unknown).

Computes a rounded integer step value from a capacity, an accumulator, and an advancement divisor plus bonus, returning 0 when the divisor is zero, though the formula's game meaning (per the SRD citation) is not fully established here.
Computes the next award level for a character by adding the step interval to the current level, or returning the current level unchanged when the interval is zero or negative.
Returns a character's age in whole years by dividing their age in days by the days-per-year constant (the SRD starts characters at 5840 days, or 16 years).
Applies the withering trap by aging the character by a fixed number of weeks (kWitheringDays, 28 days per the SRD note [c4]) through the shared ageBy routine.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs keeps.AgeBy (with keeps.DescribeDays for the "4 week(s)" wording)

what: Using Kind 25 (a stat item, possibly a potion) ages the character by 28 days, per SRD c31.
Applies the complication effect to a character by adding 15 years to their age, multiplying their maximum hit points by 0.8333 (rounded down), and capping current hit points at the new maximum.
Rounds a raw fractional game value to the nearest whole number using round-half-even, implementing the B(.) rounding rule used in rest/recovery calculations (e.g. 30.77 becomes 31).
Casts a Guild enum value to its underlying integer index, with no game rule applied.
Returns the race's experience multiplier by looking up the race's raw experience value in a table, which sets how much a character of that race's experience gains are scaled.

Computes a character's experience-point total for a given level as a quadratic in the level, scaled by the guild's XP factor and the race multiplier (the exact Fn12A1 formula is unknown, so this is an assumed one).
Computes the gold a character accrues per level from a guild's gold factor (GGF), which the code simplifies to 30.1 × GGF per level, with the level cancelling out under the assumed reading.
Returns the total XP needed to reach a given character level, scaled by the guild's experience factor and the race's experience multiplier, and rounded to a whole number.
Sums the gold needed to advance a character's guild from its current level up to a target level, rounding each step to whole gold, and returns the total in Currency units.
Returns the archive route target level for a guild, which is 28 for Warrior, 30 for Nomad, and 41 for Wizard, and 0 for any other guild since no target is defined.

Returns the archive HP gained when a character reaches a given level in a guild: Warriors get a flat average per level up to level 28, Nomads get a bonus at levels 29 and up (with a post-cap amount past their max level), and Wizards get a post-target amount past their target level, with other cases yielding 0.
Decides whether a character qualifies for the archive route's bonus hit points, which requires Constitution at least 17 and a guild level below the hits cap level.

Determines whether a given race may join a given guild in Mordor, returning false for Elves, Osiri and Gnomes as Warriors and for Giants, Morlochs and Gnomes as Wizards, and true for all other combinations.

Decides whether a character's guild membership is "pinned" (experience has reached the cap just short of the next level's threshold) and so should show the level-up announcement, optionally suppressing it when the level is already at the maximum.
Rounds a non-negative double to the nearest integer with halves rounded up by adding 0.5 and truncating via vbInt, a numeric helper used by the gold projection loop.
Returns the experience multiplier for a kill, giving companion-struck kills a reduced factor (kCompanionXpFactor, 0.25) and character-struck kills the full 1.0.
Clamps a party size to the range 1 to kPartyMaxSize and returns a multiplier that reduces XP by 4% for each member beyond the first.
Returns the index of the first unoccupied slot in a boolean occupancy vector, or -1 if all slots are taken, which lets a new character reuse a deleted roster slot.
Computes the total gold needed to advance from the current character level, summing each level's cost (scaled by the guild gold factor) with per-level rounding, and returns it in currency units.
Caps a character's maximum hit points at 999, the game's hit-point ceiling, by returning the smaller of the given value and kHitsCap.
Announces to the player that their character has enough experience to make a level, but only on the change where XP first crosses the level's requirement.
Returns true only if the character's level in the given guild is strictly higher than the level in every other guild, which implements the game's "highest guild" condition.

Computes the hit points a character gains on reaching a new level, using the guild's average hits, a Nomad-only bonus for levels in a given range, a constitution bonus below the max level, and a fixed past-max amount when the level exceeds the cap.
Computes the number of days a character must spend resting to recover, based on the percentage of hit points missing (zero days at full HP, 31 days at zero HP, rounded half-even).
Applies resting-time aging by computing the days a character ages from their current and maximum hit points, adding them to the character's age, and announcing the passage of time to the player.
Decides whether a poison-clearing attempt succeeds by checking that the roll result is above the kPoisonClearAbove threshold (185).

Applies a poison cure attempt that costs the character 2 hit points each try and, if the cure roll succeeds, clears the character's poison level and announces the poison is purged, otherwise announces that the poison remains.
Decides whether a disease clear attempt succeeds, returning true when the roll result is above the kDiseaseClearAbove threshold (195).
Applies a disease cure attempt by charging a fixed hit-point cost to the character, then clears the disease if the roll result passes and otherwise reports that it remains.
Returns true when a character's age in days has reached 98% of their race's natural lifespan, marking the onset of old age.
Computes the percent chance of natural death for a character past the old-age onset, as 5 plus the natural log of days beyond onset (floored at one day), clamped to 0–100, and returns 0 before onset.
Rolls a d100 against the character's age-based natural death chance, once old age has set in, and emits an "Old age claims the character" message if the roll succeeds.
Applies the sanctuary spell's effect by adding 365 days (the original's aging amount, or the port's constant) to the target character's age and emitting a message saying the spell aged them.
Converts a Race enum value to its underlying integer index (0 through 8, in the order Human through Troll) so it can be used to look up race table entries.
Rolls a race's base value for one stat by drawing uniformly at random between that race's minimum and maximum for that stat.
Returns the maximum value a character of the given race may reach for a given stat, which is that race's base stat maximum plus a fixed offset of 5 (the R3 rule).
Raises a character's stat by the given amount, capped at the race's maximum for that stat, and stores the result only if it actually increases.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ApplyStatMods (the class name is not shown in the candidate; the method is `ApplyStatMods`)

what: Looks up in the guild grid (table T4) whether a given race is permitted to join a given guild, returning that yes/no answer as data without the engine enforcing it.
Checks whether a given race may take a given alignment by looking up that race's alignment mask, so creating a character can reject alignments the race is not allowed to have.
Returns the percentage resistance a given race has against a given damage or effect category, looked up from the race's resistance table (categories not listed count as 0).
Applies a race's resistance percentage to an amount by reducing it by that percent, rounding the reduction half-even, and returns the remaining value.
Ages a character by one unit (ageDays += 1) per call as a placeholder for the race-dependent aging mechanic, which is not yet implemented in the source.
Returns a character's required XP scaled by their race's penalty multiplier, rounded half-even, per the game's racial XP rule (R9/R11).

Computes an approximate experience-point multiplier for a given race from that race's Exp value, using a logarithmic formula that the code notes does not match the reference table for Elf, Osiri and Troll.
Returns a race's normalized racial penalty factor r (Human = 1.0), looked up from the SRD penalty table, which feeds into the experience required for advancement.
Always returns false and ignores its item argument, so it never requires Great Strength to use an item, which looks like a placeholder for an unimplemented race-based item restriction.
Blocks an Elf character from using an item that requires great strength, returning false in that case and true otherwise.
Always returns true without using its arguments, and the source marks the monster restriction as unknown, so no monster is actually restricted.
Appends the decimal digit characters of a non-negative integer to a string buffer, with no game meaning.
Checks whether adding two currency amounts would overflow the 64-bit currency range, so a bank transaction can be refused instead of wrapping around.
Returns true when a character is an ASCII decimal digit ('0' through '9'), a character-class helper used by the currency parser.
Rounds a double to the nearest integer using round-half-to-even (banker's rounding) and returns it as an i64, with no game-specific meaning.
Returns 2 raised to the power k as a 64-bit integer by left-shifting 1, a math helper with no game meaning.
Returns true when a character is a space or tab, a whitespace check used by the gold-tag parser to skip blanks.
Returns true if the character is an ASCII decimal digit ('0' through '9'), a character-class helper used by the number parser.
Lowercases a single ASCII character by mapping 'A'–'Z' to 'a'–'z' and leaving every other character unchanged.
Maps a single hex/octal digit character to its numeric value (0–15), returning 99 for any non-digit character.
Returns whether a computed value falls within the VB Long range (-2147483648 to 2147483647), so the GoldFromTag conversion can treat out-of-range gold amounts as overflow.
Rounds a currency amount stored in 1/10000 gold to the nearest whole gold, with ties going to the even whole number (banker's rounding).
Appends the decimal text form of a 32-bit integer to a string buffer, writing a leading minus sign for negative values, with no game meaning.
Parses a string the way VB's Val() does, skipping leading blanks, reading an optional sign and leading decimal digits, and clamping the result to the i32 range, with no game meaning.
Counts how many of the given thresholds a character's level has reached (level is at or above each threshold), which determines how many swings the character gets, per the Mordor guild tables.
Returns true when a character is a space or tab, the two characters trimmed from the ends of text, and has no game meaning.

Returns true if a character is a space or one of the control characters 0x09 through 0x0D (tab, newline, vertical tab, form feed, carriage return), which mirrors .NET's whitespace set for number parsing and has no game meaning.
Checks whether a single character is an ASCII decimal digit ('0' through '9') and returns true or false, with no game meaning.
Returns the span of a string with leading and trailing trim characters removed, which is general text handling with no game meaning.
Parses a VB-style ampersand literal (&H hex, &O or bare & octal) into a 32-bit integer, applying VB's two's-complement wraparound for values above the signed range.

Converts a span of text into a clean ASCII decimal number string (stripping whitespace, group separators, and D/d exponent letters, and validating the grammar) so that strtod can parse it, returning false if the text is not a valid decimal.
Returns true when a character is a hyphen or apostrophe, which the reference's word-normalization step strips out before comparison; it has no direct game meaning.
Lowercases an ASCII letter character by mapping 'A'–'Z' to 'a'–'z' and returning the value as an integer, leaving all other characters unchanged.
Uppercases an ASCII lowercase letter by subtracting the case offset, leaving every other character unchanged, as a helper for ordinal case-insensitive comparison.
Compares two strings character by character under ASCII case folding (upper or lower), optionally skipping hyphens and apostrophes, and returns -1, 0 or 1 for ordering.
Returns a constant effect id of 0 for any spell, as a placeholder until the real SpellDef ailments field is available.
Always returns false because the SpellDef field it should check (the map/raise/bind refusal flag) is missing from the headers, so the quirk is never applied.
Maps a party-wide spell effect id (200 and up) down to its underlying real effect id by subtracting 200, leaving other ids unchanged.
Checks whether a character currently has a given game effect active by scanning the character's list of active effect ids and returning true if the effect is present.
Checks whether a character has learned a given spell by scanning their list of known spell IDs, returning true if the spell is present.
Converts a Party's position fields (x, y, dungeon level, and facing cast to i32) into a Location struct and returns it, with no game rule applied.
Moves the party to a new location by setting its x and y coordinates and dungeon level from the given Location, as used when a spell (passwall or teleport/displace) relocates the party.

Reports whether the square at a given location on the current floor has its rock flag recorded, returning false for out-of-range coordinates, which Passwall and Teleport/Displace casting use to decide whether a destination is solid stone.
Reports whether a group index is valid and the group still has living members in the encounter, which the game uses to decide if a spell or breath attack can target that group.

Determines which monster class a spell's class gate reads, using the group that was aimed at (falling back to a starting group) and returning that group's front monster's class, or -1 if the group index is out of range.
Returns the index of the first unoccupied slot in the companion array, or -1 if every slot is taken.
Counts how many of the fixed companion slots in the party array are marked occupied and returns that count.

Computes the damage of a companion's special breath, spit, or shock attack by rolling a random value within a range, adding a bonus, scaling by 0.7, and halving the effect of the target's resistance percentage.

Checks whether a character may cast a given spell right now, in order: whether the spell is known, whether the caster's level and spell points suffice, whether an anti-magic area blocks it, whether an item has charges left, and whether an aligned item matches the caster's alignment, returning a refusal reason or None.
stageB_where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs, CheckCast (labelled box.CheckCast; built from CastGate.Unfit and CastGate.Refuse)

what: Checks whether a spell cast in a mod's dungeon can go ahead for a given caster, returning a refusal (blocked by monsters on the square, an invalid or dead caster, a missing required target, or a map/raise/bind spell) or None when the cast is allowed.
When a character is engaged in combat, it sets that character's combat order to cast the given spell, so the spell becomes their action for the round; otherwise it does nothing.
stageB_where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.BecomesOrder (and CastInCombat for the setting path)

what: For a monster spell, it sets the turn's damage total to the spell's damage value, replacing any damage already accumulated that turn rather than adding to it.
Picks which monster group a spell hits: the group the caster aimed at if it still has living members, otherwise the first group that still has living members, or -1 if none do.
Resolves a companion's opening spell group at the moment of casting by delegating to spellStartGroup with a -1 argument, which sets the group that the companion's spell takes effect in.
Advances a loop's step counter by one each iteration and also bumps the processed-group counter when the current slot held a group, which is generic loop bookkeeping with no game meaning of its own.
Decides whether the damage-spell group loop keeps going, returning true while fewer groups have been hit than the spell's Damage1 count and the loop is still within the four fixed damage slots.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs CastDamage (candidate 1, a private method that holds the group loop)

what: Resolves a damage spell cast against the foe groups in an encounter, walking the groups from the start group onward, applying damage to each living group (with a companion-immunity check that cancels the spell), and reporting which groups were reached, whether anything was hit, and the resulting target mark.
Returns the magic resistance percentage (clamped to 0–100) that a victim uses against a spell, or 0 if the spell's resistIndex is negative, meaning the spell has no resistance roll.

Applies the sequence of checks that decide whether a spell's effect lands on a given creature (magic immunity, charm-proof bit, all-or-nothing and charm sparing based on whether the damage kills, and the class gate), returning the verdict for that victim.
Decides whether a spell effect applies to a given monster, so effects 75–99 only hit monsters of the matching class (effect 75 targets class 0), and otherwise lets the effect through.
Shows the player a caption for each group the damage spell reached, plus a "Failed!" message if the cast did nothing.
Heals a character by a spell-healing roll computed from the spell's base, special effect, and level, capping the resulting current hit points at the character's maximum hit points.
Heals a companion party member by a rolled amount (via spellHealRoll) and caps the result at the companion's maximum Hits.
General Cure removes poison and disease from the target character and announces "Cured."
Cures poison in a character by clearing their poison level to zero and announcing "Poison cured."
Cures a character's disease by setting their disease level to zero and announcing "Disease cured." to the player.
Cure Paralysis, when the caster is paralysed, clears the caster's paralysis level and paralysed status and says "Paralysis cured," regardless of which character the player picked as the target.
Computes a spell's protection value at cast time as one plus half the caster's spell level, rounded down (Protection = Int(CasterSpellLevel / 2) + 1).
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/SpellThrown.cs Companion.Apply (the `Apply` method; its doc comment states Protection is the caster's spell level halved plus one, citing MAINMOD2.BAS:1046)

what: Computes the spell Protection value a guild gets on recompute as half its guild Level, rounded down, plus 1 (rule R29).
Computes a companion's caster level from their guild level as one sixth of it (rounded down), clamped to the range 1 to 255.
Decides whether a companion's spell fails because it is a heal with no affect group, and if so tells the player "Comp. #N failed in casting."
Returns true when a companion's spell aimed at foes is blocked because the caster itself has magic immunity, per the rule R34 quirk noted in the source.

Decides whether the breath-weapon sweep effect applies to a non-aimed group attack, which it does when the attack's special-flags bit is set and the attacker's guild level is below the sweep limit of 40.

Computes the damage of a companion's R37 breath attack by taking the special hit range from the attacker's and target's levels, adding a quarter of that range, and applying the target's resist percentage.
Computes spit and electrocution damage for a companion by taking half the special hit range between attacker and target levels, then applying the target's resistance percentage.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/SpecialHits.cs Kind.Raw (resistance comes from Mordor.Core/SpecialHits.cs Kind.AfterResistance, used in Mordor.Core/Combat.cs left.CompanionSpits)

what: Computes a monster caster's spell level as a quarter of the monster's guild level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 255.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs MonsterAttack (class containing `MonsterSpellHits`; the method is private, so the class name is not confirmed here)

what: Computes the damage a monster's spell deals to a party member, returning 0 if the target is a companion with the magic-immune bit set or if the spell is all-or-nothing and the damage falls short of the target's hit points.
Returns the percent chance that an acid spit lands, which is 90 if the character's guild level is more than 25% above the monster's, 10 if it is more than 25% below, and 50 otherwise.
Rolls a percentage chance, using the acid spit chance derived from the monster's and character's guild levels, to decide whether an acid spit attack succeeds.
Computes the acid spit damage a monster inflicts on a character, derived from the monster's and character's guild levels with a random roll, and scaled by 0.7.
Decides whether a charm spell can add another creature to the party by checking that fewer than the maximum number of companion slots are currently filled.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs, CastDamage (enclosing class not shown in the candidate)

what: Builds the companion record for a creature charmed by a spell, copying the foe's identity, alignment, and special flags and setting its current and maximum hits and binding level from the cast.
Credits the caster with one kill when a charmed creature is taken, per game rule R49 (a charmed creature counts as a kill with no hits), by incrementing the caster's kill count.
Reads a spell's displacement or teleport offsets from a list of values (Right, Forward, and Down for teleport only), failing if fewer than two values are given.

Computes the grid location a spell effect lands on by offsetting the caster's or target's position by a number of squares to the right, forward, and down relative to the facing direction, wrapping the x and y coordinates around the grid edges.

Decides where a creature or party lands after a teleport or displacement: a destination at level 0 or above results in falling from the sky, a level beyond the dungeon's maximum or a rock square results in being driven into rock, and anything else arrives safely.

Teleports or displaces the party by a spell's offset from its facing, first deciding whether the arrival lands safely, is blocked by rock, or falls from the sky, and then moving the party and applying the arrival consequences and the spell's point cost.

Casting Passwall moves the party one square forward in the caster's facing direction, then checks the landed square's rock and dungeon level to decide the arrival outcome, and charges the spell's point cost.

Applies the rock-death effect that kills the entire party on a rock square: every member is marked as dead by rock with zero hit points, their bodies are left on that square of the floor, the party is flagged as wiped, and the player is told the party is crushed.

Settles where a spell's caster ends up after a teleport or displacement: rock arrival kills the caster, a fall from the sky does nothing, and otherwise the caster's spell points are reduced by the spell's cost (floored at zero) and the party is marked as having arrived by spell.
Returns the absolute value of a 32-bit integer, with no game meaning.
Maps a relative compass direction enum value to its lowercase English word ("north", "south-west", etc.), falling back to "north" for unrecognized values.

Casting the Ethereal Portal spell walks the party into solid rock, killing the whole party if the caster is in slot 0 or 1, or only the caster and the members behind them if the caster is in slot 2 or later.

Classifies where a target stands relative to the locator, returning "too far" if the dungeon levels differ by more than the locate range, "in the city" if the target is in the city area, and otherwise a relative compass direction.

Announces to the player, via localized messages, where each other saved character is located relative to the caster (too far away, in the city, or in a compass direction) when the Locate spell is cast.

Lists the indices of dead characters whose death was caused by rock (a stoning-type death state) and who are on the party leader's dungeon level and in the city area, which is the candidate set for the fetch spell's target selection.
Tests whether a body's dungeon level is deeper than kFetchMaxDungeonLevel, returning true when it is within reach for the fetch spell.

Attempts a spell that retrieves a chosen roster character to the caster's square, level, and area and marks them saved, provided the pick is a valid candidate and the character is within reach of the dungeon level; a cancel or out-of-list pick spends nothing.
Decides whether a companion can be a candidate for binding, which is true only when it is still alive (Hits > 0) and has a nonzero BindingLevel.
Collects the indices of every companion in the list for which `isBindCandidate` returns true, returning them as a vector.
Fate re-rolls a character's current hit points and current spell points, each as a uniform random value from 1 up to its maximum, and announces the new values to the player.
Builds the sanctuary point for the party's current position by offsetting the stored X and Y coordinates by one and recording the party's dungeon level, which is the location a sanctuary spell marks.
Casts the Sanctuary spell by recording the caster's current party position (x, y, and dungeon level) as the sanctuary point and announcing to the player that sanctuary is set there.
Returns a character to sanctuary: if no sanctuary point was ever set it reports that and does nothing, otherwise it ages the caster by kSanctuaryDays and reports the return.
Adds the given number of days to a character's age in days, which is the ageing mechanic (R63) of the game.

Ends the party's lost state for all facings, levels, and position, clears each member's lost status, and announces that the party is no longer lost (the effect of the Depth Perception and Find Direction spells).

Builds a spell's sheet from its definition, mapping its damage values to base and power, flagging it as blank when both are zero, clamping its kill-effect index into the 0–8 verb range, and classing it as Detrimental or Beneficial by its effect when it has damage.
Computes the natural logarithm of a value, returning 0 for non-positive inputs (the sheet leaves that case undefined), which feeds into the game's spell-magnitude and scaling formulas.
Converts a double to a 64-bit integer by truncating toward zero, with no game meaning.
Looks up a spell definition by index in the game data's spell list, returning a pointer to it or null if the index is out of range.

Computes a spell's scaled magnitude (damage or healing) from its base value G, the caster's level or spell level S, and a logarithmic growth term, following the Mordor spell-damage and healing formulas.

Computes the archive minimum for a spell's damage or healing, combining a base value, a logarithmic term scaled by spell level, and a power-dependent term, then averaging the three (per the R10 and R13 formulas in the Mordor spell rules).
Rolls a random value of the given minimum plus 1 to the minimum (in game terms, a damage or heal roll per SRD R10/R13), with the span clamped to at least 1.
Returns the (dx, dy) step for moving forward and the (dx, dy) step for moving to the right from a given facing direction (N, E, S, or W), used to turn relative movement into map offsets.
Computes the damage modifier for a damage spell at a given spell level, scaling the base and power values with a log term LN(SL+1) to produce the damage figure the engine applies.
Computes the healing magnitude of a spell from its base value, power, and spell level, using the scaled-magnitude formula with the heal base constant.
Computes a spell's magnitude for a given spell level, returning a blank result when the spell's Base is blank and otherwise the damage and heal modifiers derived from its base and power terms.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.SpellDamage (and Rules.SpellHeal, which uses the same base/power/level formula)

what: Computes the damage range of a detrimental spell from its magnitude, giving a minimum of half the damage modifier minus one and a maximum of the full modifier minus one, and returns no range for blank magnitudes or beneficial spells.

Computes the Beneficial spell's heal range in Mordor (per SRD R4), giving a minimum of ROUNDDOWN(healMod × 0.5 − 1) and a maximum of ROUNDDOWN(healMod × 1 − 1), and returns no range for blank magnitudes or non-beneficial spells.
Reports whether the HP note should be shown for a spell, which requires both that a damage range exists and that the spell row's HP flag is "Y".
Computes a sheet base value for a character attribute by multiplying Q and R by the sheet factor (1.9), subtracting a small epsilon, and truncating to an integer, per SRD rule R6.

Scales a spell's base magnitude by the caster's sheet factors (C × Q × R × kSheetFactor divided by SL, minus a small epsilon, floored), never letting the result drop below the base value, and returns the base unchanged if SL is zero or negative.
Computes the Mordor sheet column value K from the SRD R7 formula, rounding up C·Q·R·1.9/(C+1) and returning twice that minus one, though its in-game purpose is unknown.
Looks up a combat spell's monster and group targeting caps (numM and numG) from its spell definition, returning zeros if the spell index is invalid.

Determines a spell's reach in combat: whole-party spells (effect 200 and up), class-filtered charm and control spells (effects 75-99), monster-targeting combat spells (effects 0 and 100), and caster-only spells otherwise, defaulting to caster-only when the spell is missing.

Determines the verb shown for a spell's effect in the game: a kill spell (effect 100) reads "KILLED", a charm spell (effect 80–99) reads "CHARMED", and any other spell uses its data-file verb index, or NONE if the spell or index is invalid.
Computes the minimum damage of an archive-style damage spell from its base value, power, and spell level, using the R10 formula (averaging base and a level-scaled term).
Rolls a spell's base damage as the minimum value plus a random amount from 1 up to that minimum, per SRD rule R10.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.SpellDamage (nearest spell-damage routine, but it does not match)

what: Computes a resisted spell or attack damage by scaling the base damage down by the target's resistance percentage and rounding half to even, as the game's R10 formula defines.
Decides whether a kill spell succeeds in Mordor by comparing the rolled damage against the monster's hit points, so the spell kills only if the damage is at least the monster's HP.
Computes the minimum heal amount for an archive (healing) spell from its base value, power, and spell level, using the R13 formula with a fixed divisor.
Rolls a healing amount for a spell by adding a random value from 1 to the minimum to the minimum itself, per the SRD's healing formula (R13).
Computes an item's protection (Defense) value from its SL as 3 × (LN SL)², per R15 of the Mordor rules.
Computes the guild spell protection Defense value for a given spell level as 3 × ln(⌊SL/2⌋ + 1)², reproducing the source's known-buggy formula as written.
Charms up to the capped number of monster groups' front creatures matching the given monster class, marking them charmed, non-hostile, and their groups Peaced, and reports success or failure.
When a Control Dragon spell fails, the targeted monster group turns hostile and loses its charmed status, and the player is told the targets respond adversely.
Sets the player's Sanctuary location in the store by copying the given position and dungeon level, then announces that the location is set.
Sanctuary, once Set Sanctuary has been cast, returns the party to the stored location and ages the caster by a fixed number of days; with no stored location it prints "Nothing happens" and fails.

Displaces the party by a given number of squares to the right and ahead of its facing inside the dungeon, while outside the dungeon it instead destroys the whole party as the spell's rule (R20) requires.

Ethereal Portal (R20) moves the caster two squares forward through the wall in front, by calling the shared displacement routine with a 0 offset and a distance of 2, and stops rather than hanging if rock lies behind the wall.
Linear search over the kMovementSpellRows table to return the row matching a given movement spell, or nullptr if no row matches.

Returns the scope in which a movement spell can be cast, making it usable in combat only when the spell's table row is flagged as combat-usable (only Teleport, per the comment), and non-combat otherwise or if the spell has no row.
Looks up a movement spell's row in a table by its id and returns that row's base spell level, or 0 if the spell has no row.

Checks whether a character's current Intelligence, Wisdom, and Constitution meet the stat requirements to cast a given movement spell, where only Sanctuary has requirements and all other movement spells are always castable.
Computes the chance that a teleport spell cast in combat sends an enemy into rock, as 100 minus the creature's magic resistance clamped to 0–100 (a guessed formula, since the SRD gives none).
Teleport-in-combat spell: sends up to a capped number of monsters away from an encounter, one group at a time, rolling a per-monster chance to impale each one into rock.

Computes the spell damage modifier for a Mordor spell at a given spell level, adding the base damage, a logarithmic level-scaled term (LN(SL+1)/LN(5)), and a truncated power term, with spell levels below 1 treated as 1.
Caps a spell level to the range 1 to 255 so that the effective spell level used for spell damage and healing stays within the game's limits (a spell level of 0 counts as 1).
Rolls the second modifier for a spell in the Mordor rules (R6 step 2), taking a random value scaled by the first modifier and the spell level, truncated toward zero, and adds 1.
Looks up a crest's spell grant in the R10 table, returning the row for that crest, or a row with no spell and zero if the crest (such as Journeyman, Warrior, or Ninja) has no entry.
Grants a crest its spell, if the crest has one in the table, by returning that spell with its charges and the caster's current spell level, and posts a "Crest grants a spell" message.

Resolves a movement or utility spell cast by a living party member, such as Detect Rock on the wall ahead, Feather Essence levitating a target, or an Ethereal Portal or Displacement that can kill the whole party.
Clamps an integer value `v` into the inclusive range [lo, hi], returning the nearest bound when it falls outside.
Returns the larger of two 32-bit integers, a generic math helper with no game meaning.
Clamps a value to the range between a lower and upper bound, returning the lower bound if the value is below it, the upper bound if above it, and the value itself otherwise.
Returns the smaller of two doubles, a generic math helper with no game meaning.
Returns the larger of two numbers, which callers use to take the greater of two stone-related chance or value figures when resolving petrification in the game.
Rolls a uniform random d100 (1 to 100) from the game's RNG, used for percentile checks in the status-effect rules such as poison, disease, paralysis, petrification, and aging.
Returns the character's Constitution score from their ability stats, which the status-effect rules (poison, disease, paralysis, stoning, drain, aging) use as an input.
Computes a character's effective Constitution for status-effect checks by adding the gear-granted CON bonus to base CON, following the SRD legend rather than the port's gear-less tick.
Returns the value of one ability stat from a character's stat array, looked up by the stat's index.

Returns the character's resistance value for the given index (the resistance slot indexed by idx), which status-effect checks such as poison, disease, paralysis and petrification use to decide whether an effect takes hold.
Returns whether a given bit position is set in a 32-bit flags value, a generic bit-test helper with no game meaning.
Forwards a status-event code and text string to the context's message sink with empty numeric payloads, so the caller can report a status effect without supplying any numbers.
Rolls a poison-resistance check against the victim and, if the victim fails and is not already poisoned, sets their poison level to the attacker's level and posts a "Poisoned" message.

Rolls a disease-resistance check against the victim's disease resistance and, if the victim fails and is not already diseased, sets their disease level to the attacker's level and notes that they have been diseased.
Reports whether a character is held in place by paralysis, which is true whenever their paralysis level is above zero (rule R16).
Returns true unless the character is held (paralyzed or otherwise immobilized), so a held character takes no action on its own turn while companions still act.
Returns true (refusing the action) whenever the character is held, except for taking the stairs down or the chute, which are allowed.

Computes the ailment roll offset for a character from their effective Constitution (relative to a base of 10, weighted) minus a penalty scaled by level, which feeds into the chance of resisting poison, disease, and similar status effects.
For a monster's melee attack, applies poison to the victim and then disease, each resolved against the attacker's level.
While the character has a disease (diseaseLevel above zero), any healing they receive is halved, rounded down.
Cures poison on a character when they rest in town, but only if they currently have a poison level above zero.
Computes a character's chance to resist a melee paralysis attack as their paralysis resistance plus Constitution, capped at 95.
Makes a melee paralysis saving throw against a character after a damaging monster hit, and if the save fails while no paralysis rounds are pending, applies paralysis to the character.
On each four-second tick, rolls d100 against the paralysis wear-off chance for a held character and, if the roll exceeds it, ends the paralysis.
Ends paralysis on a character when no monster occupies the square, as the game's R20 rule dictates, and reports whether it did so.
Applies the monster group special-attack effects (breath, acid spit, electrocution, and melee side effects like poison) against one party member, rolling chances and damage per the game's rules.

Reduces a monster's special-attack damage by a resistance percentage (half the resistance value, applied as a fraction of the damage, rounded down), leaving damage unchanged when resistance is zero or negative.
Classifies a monster-versus-character level comparison into High, Low, or Even bands using 0.75× and 1.25× thresholds, which feeds game mechanics such as breath and spit attack chances.
Returns the breath-weapon threshold percentage (80, 50, or 20) for a monster, chosen by comparing the highest guild level against the monster's level through a ratio band lookup.
Returns the spit-attack chance threshold percentage (90, 50, or 10) for a monster, chosen by comparing the active level to the monster's level via a ratio band lookup.

Rolls the damage dealt by a monster's breath attack, derived from the monster's guild level and the victim's active level, with a random factor, returning 0 if the attack's base value is not positive.

what: Rolls the damage dealt by a monster's spit attack, scaled by the monster's guild level and the victim's active level, with a random factor and a final rounding step.
Returns the electrocution chance percentage (90, 50, or 10) by looking up the band that the character's level relative to the monster's level falls into.
Computes the stoning chance for a target as its Constitution times a log-based factor, minus the attacker's level, capped at a maximum value.
Rolls a d100 against the target's stoning chance and, if the roll exceeds it, marks the character as Stoned and records a status message.
Computes a companion's stone value from its Constitution score via a logarithmic formula (CON × ln(max(1, CON)) / ln 2.5), minus a floor amount, per the R30 rule.
Rolls a percentage check against a companion-derived stone value, and if the roll fails the target becomes stoned and loses all its hits.

Rolls a number of drain trials (scaled by the attacker's level), lets each trial be resisted by the target's drain resistance or Constitution-based save, and collects Table E drain picks for each trial that fails.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs CombatEngine.GroupAttacks (closest, but it only lists drain as one step in a monster group's turn)

what: Applies a Table E drain result from a monster's special attack: a pick of 1–5 lowers the matching ability stat by 1, and a pick of 6 lowers the character's maximum hits by the drain amount, with a note logged either way.
Computes the aging saving-throw chance for a character as 2.5 times their base Constitution minus 2 times the monster's floor level, as a rule from the game's aging mechanic.

When a character fails a save against a monster's aging attack, it rolls a random number of days (up to 365 times a monster-level-based multiplier, capped at 1825) and adds them to the character's age.

Checks whether a character is petrified by making two successive saving throws against stone resistance, with the second save's threshold derived from the target's Constitution and the monster's floor, and sets the character to Stoned on failing both.

Computes the chance that a character survives a destruction save, starting from a base of 45, lowered by the monster's floor value, raised by four times the character's DEX, lowered by twice the monster's DEX, and clamped between 25 and 90.
Rolls a save against a destruction chance for a random pack slot 1–39, and if the save fails and that slot holds an item, clears it and announces "Item destroyed."
Computes a theft score for a thief by adding a random roll (0–99) to a level-and-coefficient-based bonus, then adds half that score again when the victim is defending.
Decides whether a theft of gold is attempted by checking if the thief's score minus a weighted monster guild level penalty falls below a threshold (rule R36).
Returns a random item slot number between 2 and 40 (inclusive) for item theft, using the game context's RNG, so the chosen slot can fall outside the pack.

Computes the damage an archive-form electrocution or acid attack deals to a character, scaling with the monster's guild level, reduced by character level, and cut by the character's resistance percentage (floored at zero).
Computes the damage of an archive breath attack from the monster's guild level, rolling a random value in a range scaled by the target's resistance percentage (halved, then applied as a reduction).
Computes the chance that an archive stone effect triggers, starting from 100 plus the spawn level and subtracting a CON-based penalty (CON·ln(CON)·1.09), clamped to a minimum floor value.
Computes the percent chance that an archive paralysis effect takes hold on a target, as 100 minus the sum of their resistance and Constitution, never dropping below a fixed floor of 5.
Computes the chance that a character's archive (spawned item or record) ages, as 100 plus twice the spawn level minus 2.5 times the Constitution, truncated to an integer.
Casts a signed 32-bit integer to an unsigned 32-bit integer, a bit-level conversion with no game meaning.
Returns the value of a single ability stat from a character's stats array, looking it up by the stat's index.
Emits a "char.save" event with a "Character saved." message for the given character, leaving the actual persistence to code outside the core.
Presents a rescue offer to the player by emitting a "rescue.offer" message naming the character, leaving the actual presentation to the host.
Applies the chest poison-gas trap: each party member rolls against their poison resistance, and on failure becomes poisoned at the party's dungeon level.
Applies the disease-spores chest trap (R38): each party member rolls against half their Disease resistance, and on a hit becomes diseased at the party's dungeon level.
Implements the chest trap 6 (Fate) from the Mordor rules, rerolling the opener's current hit points and then current spell points to random values between 1 and their maximums.
Chest trap 8 (Blackout) wipes every active spell effect from the character who opened the chest.
Rolls the ambient sound check for a dungeon tick, which succeeds with a flat percent chance only when nothing is in front of the party.

Applies the R42 water/quicksand hazard to a non-levitating character by subtracting the hazard level from their current hits, and on quicksand may roll (R43) to pick a random pack slot whose item the caller should destroy.
Decides whether a character dies of old age by returning true once their age in days reaches the race's maximum age (a deterministic placeholder for the unsupplied R42 step 2f formula).
Rolls the first-pass chance to recognise an unidentified foe, using the character's identify skill from guild level, Int and Wis, and marks the foe as identified on success unless it is unseen.

Runs the identification pass over each non-empty monster group in the front encounter, calling the first and second identification passes on each group's front monster during the R42 step 2a sequence.

Clears a character's paralysis, poison, disease, and spell resistance levels, implementing the game's EndEveryAilment effect (the stone/DeathState is left alone and the stat part of paralysis is not restored).
After a party member dies in a party of more than one, this saves that character, removes the dead from the party, and refreshes the party display for the player, with no rescue offered.
When a lone character (party of one) dies, the function saves the character and then offers them a rescue, per rule R48.

When a character dies in a party of one, this marks them dead if they aren't already, runs the lone-death flow and rescue handling, and emits a raise offer if a raise is pending; in a larger party it instead prunes the dead from the party.
Handles a character's death outside of combat by passing the dying character's slot and the cause of death to killCharacter, which applies the death to the party and companion roster.
Handles a character who is rescued after being lost in the dungeon: adds the days spent waiting to their age, cures any poison, moves them to town, and announces they were carried home.

what: Resolves a rock death from the 1995 Mordor rules (R54): when a caster in the party triggers it, the caster and the members after them (plus those before them if the caster is in slot 0 or 1) are killed by rock, with automap records and a "walked into solid rock" message logged.

Runs one companion's per-tick check in the dungeon: a companion with binding below 100 may drift one point toward zero and, if it drifts, may then leave the party, a binding of zero always makes it leave, and a companion whose alignment opposes its owner's may defect to the hostile side, with the result reported back to the caller.
Rolls the R56 defection check for an opposed companion, with a percent chance of defecting if the companion is Evil (kDefectChanceEvil) or Neutral (kDefectChanceNeutral) and never defecting if Good.
Rolls a drift check for a companion by comparing a random draw scaled by 200 against the given drift value, returning true when the drift threshold is met.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/CompanionMood.cs CompanionMood.Step.Round (Candidate 3, with Step.Drift as its drift-threshold helper)

what: Rolls a random number and returns true if it falls under the leave threshold (the check that passes when the roll times 200 is less than leaveValue), which decides whether a companion leaves the party.

Computes a companion's chance to leave its owner, combining the monster's guild level, the owner's top guild level, the binding value, the companion's natural Charisma, and how wounded it is, then clamps the result between 0 and the maximum leave chance.
Rounds a floating-point value to the nearest integer using round-half-to-even, with no game meaning attached.
Returns a reference to the party member at the given index, converting the signed index to an unsigned one for container access, with no game rule applied.
Returns a read-only reference to the party member at a given signed index, converting the index to unsigned for container access, with no game rule applied.

Rolls d100 against a character's resistance to poison or disease and, if the roll beats it while the affliction level is still zero, sets the affliction level and announces the affliction to the player.
Classifies a victim's level against a reference level using 1.25x and 0.75x ratio bands (Table D), returning the high, mid, or low outcome used by breath, spit, and electrocution effects.
Rerolls a random value from 1 to max using the game's RNG, as used for chest fate (Table F), and returns 0 if max is not positive.
Maps a DeathCause enum value to a fixed English phrase describing how the character died, for use in death messages.
Sets a character's death state, zeroes their current hit points, and increments their death count, without producing any message for the player.
Returns the percentage resistance a character has against a given resist kind, or 0 if the index is out of range.

Attempts to poison a character: a resistance roll against the Poison resistance decides whether the character becomes poisoned at the found level, with the poisoned status and message applied if the roll fails.

Rolls a disease-resistance check against the character's Resistance (stat 4) and, if the character fails while not already diseased, sets their disease level to the level where it was found and shows the "You have caught a disease!" message.

Computes the percent chance that a paralysis effect lands on a character by adding the resistance percentage to the character's CON, then clamping the result between a floor and a cap (the floor and cap constants are defined elsewhere).

Clears the paralysed status, its paralysis level, and its paralysis round counter when the character reaches the city gate, while leaving lost stats unrestored, and sends the "paralysis leaves you" message.
Clamps a monster's tick save chance (per Table K) to the range 5 to 90, so the value can never fall below 5% or rise above 90%.
Blocks a paralysed character from taking the stairs up, while allowing them to go down.
Casts the Cure Paralysis spell on the caster, which fails during combat and otherwise removes the paralysis from them.
Computes the bonus added to a poison or disease cure roll from the character's effective Constitution (above or below 10, doubled) minus twice the ailment's level, per Table F.
Rolls a d200 with a cure bonus based on Constitution and poison level, and the poison is cured if the roll exceeds 185.
Rolls a disease cure check, adding the character's effective Constitution bonus and subtracting twice the poison level from a d200 roll, and reports the cure as successful when the total exceeds 195.

Each tick, if the character is poisoned and alive, it rolls to cure the poison using Constitution and poison level; on failure it takes poison damage, and if hit points drop to zero or below the character dies of poison.

Each round a character with disease rolls a cure check, reduced by poison when the poison was not cured this tick; on failure the disease removes hit points, and the character dies if hit points reach zero.
When a character dies, runs the death routine and, if the party can be rescued, flags the party as awaiting rescue and tells the player someone may be able to find them.
When a party member dies, this clears all of that member's ailments (status effects) by calling endEveryAilment on them.

Decides whether a party death in the party window offers the player rescue, returning true only when the party has more than one member (a port quirk noted as possibly differing from the original game).
Drowning a party member clears their paralysis, poison and disease, then sets them to Dead, with no death text shown here.
Applies the rock death outcome to a party member by killing the character with the Rock death state and cause, flagged as a rule-driven death.
Rolls two percentile checks against the character's Constitution-based stoning chance and stone resistance, and returns true only if both fail, meaning the character is turned to stone.
Each tick with no monster in front, rolls a flat 10% chance to print a "distant sound" message to the player, and returns whether it fired.
Tests whether a given bit is set in a 32-bit flags word by shifting the flags right by the bit's index and masking the lowest bit.

Returns the breath-weapon damage percentage for a monster based on the ratio of the victim's level to the monster's guild level, using Table D bands (80% above 1.25x, 50% between 0.75x and 1.25x, 20% below 0.75x).
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.CompanionBreathes (the inline 80/50/20 quarter-band selection, not a standalone method)

what: Returns the spit attack's chance percentage for a victim, picked from high, mid, or low bands by comparing the victim's level against the monster guild's level (Table D).
Returns the percent chance that a victim of a given level is electrocuted, using the monster-spit percentage bands (high, mid, low) and the monster level as the reference level.
stageB_where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.LevelGapChance (the class name is inferred from the file, since the candidate header shows only `of.LevelGapChance`)

what: Rolls a random number of aging days for a monster, capped at 365 times a scale factor derived from the monster's guild level (clamped between 1 and 5).
Makes a percentile drain saving throw by rolling d100 and returning true (resisted) when the roll is at or below the character's drain resistance percentage.
Maps a d6 draw to a Table E drain result: draws 1 to 5 drain the matching stat index by 1, draw 6 drains MaxHits by 2, and anything else drains nothing.
Rolls a d6 on the drain table (Table E) and returns the drain result that the roll maps to.

Applies a stat or maximum-hits drain from a status effect to the character, lowering max hits (capping current hits to match) or reducing an ability stat by the drained amount, and announces the result to the player.
Chest trap 6 ("Fate") rerolls the character's current hit points and spell points to random values between 1 and their maximums, then tells the player.
Rolls a percentile check against the character's poison resistance and, if it fails, sets the character's poison level to the dungeon level, which is the Poison Gas trap's effect in the Mordor rules.

Rolls a percentile check against the character's disease resistance (resistance 4 for the Disease Spores chest trap) and, on failure, sets the character's disease level to the dungeon level, returning whether they were afflicted.
Halves a character's healing amount, rounding down, while the character has a disease (diseaseLevel above zero), and otherwise returns the heal unchanged.
Applies a cure spell to a character by removing poison and disease, and for the Cure spell also restoring missing hits (halved while diseased, with the amount left unresolved per Table H).
Resting in town cures poison by clearing the character's poison level to zero and showing the player a "The poison leaves you in town" message, doing nothing if they are not poisoned.
Looks up a spell name against the killed-spell and drained-spell lists and returns whether that spell kills outright, drains levels, or has no such effect.
Linearly searches the game's item list for the entry whose id matches the given value and returns a pointer to it, or null if none matches.

Reports whether an item type is sold by the charge-chunk (such as potions and scrolls) in the General Store, based on its charge count and item type, which is store stock logic from the reference rules.
Clamps an integer to the store's shelf capacity limit (kStoreShelfCap), returning the value unchanged unless it exceeds that cap.
Computes the gold fee charged to realign an item's alignment, at 72% of its base price (doubled when more than one alignment step is requested), rounded half-even and returned in currency units.
